# Clearer audit results

## Problem statement

The audit skill's end-of-session report Conclusion section buries the readiness
verdict ("Ready for ship") at the end of a long sentence, making it easy for
operators to miss when scanning reports. The verdict needs to be visually
prominent so operators can instantly see whether the item is ready to ship or
not.

## Users

- **Operators** reviewing audit results need to see at a glance whether the
  audited item is ready to ship.
- **Producers** scanning a grid of panes need the verdict to be immediately
  visible in the Conclusion section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the session status is `completed`, the Conclusion section's first line
   is `✅ Ready to ship` (green) on its own line, followed by the completion
   sentence: `This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}).`
2. When the session status is **not** `completed`, the Conclusion section's
   first line is `🚫 Not ready to ship` (red) on its own line, followed by the
   incomplete-session sentence.
3. The green and red colouring is applied via ANSI escape sequences so that
   terminals supporting colour display the text in the correct colour, while
   plain-text terminals degrade gracefully (no garbled output).
4. All existing end-of-session reports across all skills (audit, intake, plan,
   implement, ship, …) use the new Conclusion format.
5. All existing tests for `render_report.py` pass; new tests cover the
   green/red colour formatting in both completed and incomplete states.

## Impact

Operators can now see at a glance whether an audited item is ready to ship by
looking at the colour and position of the verdict in the audit's Conclusion
section.

## Constraints

- The report renderer must work in plain-text (non-ANSI) terminals — colour
  is best-effort.
- The change must be backward-compatible with existing report consumers that
  parse the Conclusion section.
- The `next_action` parameter should no longer be appended at the end of the
  completion sentence (it is replaced by the standalone "Ready to ship" /
  "Not ready to ship" line).

## Existing state

The `render_report()` function in
`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` builds the Conclusion section as:

```
## Conclusion

This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}.
```

For incomplete sessions:

```
## Conclusion

{skill_name} session for {id} ({title}) is incomplete. Requires attention ({next_action}).
```

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Modify the `render_report()`
  function's Conclusion section to move the readiness verdict to the top,
  in green or red.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update existing tests and add
  new tests for the colour-coded Conclusion format.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via
  helper report skill (the skill that introduced the report template).
- SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)
- SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB – Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill release process (completed)
- SA-0MQ01F8OJ007HEEP – Test: AMPA audit handler writes to audit_results via wl audit-set (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What format should the "not ready" message use? — Answer: "Not ready to ship" with red colour, mirroring the "Ready to ship" green format. Source: work item description ("or its negative counterpart").
- Q: Should the `next_action` parameter still appear in the Conclusion? — Answer: No — it is replaced by the standalone verdict line. Source: work item description says to "move" the readiness line to appear first.

# A no-op finish finalised an item whose acceptance criteria were unmet

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` marks a work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal) even
when its worktree produced **no commit attributable to the item** and its
acceptance criteria were never exercised (e.g. an operational run that must
happen on its own schedule). On that no-op path the report attributes the
ambient `dev` HEAD — a hash belonging to a *different* work item — as "the
commit", so a parent whose child carries zero work is advanced to `in_review`:
a silent false positive that hides unmet ACs from the producer and the audit
skill.

## Users

- **Driven child sessions / agents**: a session whose worktree is clean
  (first session died before writing, or the item legitimately waits on an
  external window) must never see its item silently finalised with no work.
- **Producers / operators**: must be able to trust `in_review` — it means the
  ACs are actually met. A false `in_review` hides outstanding criteria.
- **Audit skill**: reads terminal state to decide what to verify; a false
  terminal hides a genuinely unmet AC5-style operational criterion.
- **Verification-only items** (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): items whose only
  deliverable is *running* a measurement and recording evidence — the
  legitimate no-op-push path must keep working, now behind an explicit signal.

### User stories

- As a producer, when a child was finalised with zero commits and no
  acceptance evidence, I want the item to stay open with a loud explanation,
  so `in_review` never hides unmet ACs (the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM cascade is
  impossible).
- As an agent running `finish`, when I legitimately complete a
  verification-only item with no code change, I want an explicit
  `--verification-only` flag that finalises it and reports "no changes, no
  commit" — never a commit hash belonging to someone else's work.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — No-op finish refuses the terminal write by default.** When
  `phase_finish` detects its worktree produced no commit attributable to the
  item (clean-tree/no-diff path) and no `--verification-only` signal is
  present, it must **not** write `status=completed`/`stage=in_review`: the
  item stays in its prior state, `finish` fails (or reports loudly) with an
  actionable message, and no "Implementation complete. Commit \<sha\>" comment
  is posted using an ambient/unrelated HEAD.
- **AC2 — Commit attribution is never false.** `finish`'s completion report
  may only name a commit that is attributable to this item (created by this
  finish run or a prior run of this item's worktree). On the no-commit path it
  must say "no changes / no commit", naming the retained worktree and any
  recorded evidence instead of the ambient `dev` HEAD.
- **AC3 — Verification-only path preserved behind an explicit flag.** An
  explicit opt-in (e.g. `implement.py finish <id> --verification-only`) still
  finalises a no-commit item to `completed`/`in_review`, exactly preserving
  the behaviour pinned by `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`
  (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): terminal status persists and the store read-back
  assertion still passes, but the report names "no changes" and never
  misattributes a hash.
- **AC4 — drive/phase_parent never presents zero work as finishable.** A child
  whose worktree exists but carries no commit attributable to the item and no
  verification-only signal is classified as "no work / not finalisable":
  `drive`/`phase_parent` does **not** run `finish` on it, reports it as such
  (child stays open), and the parent is **not** advanced to `in_review`.
  Finish's own refusal (AC1) remains the defence in depth for direct
  invocation.
- **AC5 — Automated regression coverage.** Unit/integration tests cover:
  (i) commit-vs-no-op distinction in `git_commit`, (ii) the default refusal
  path (AC1), (iii) the `--verification-only` path (AC3) including the
  existing no-diff status regression pin, and (iv) the drive/phase_parent
  classification (AC4).
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (and any related
  implement-skill docs) documents the new no-op semantics, the
  `--verification-only` flag, and how the agent should treat a clean,
  commit-less worktree.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Preserve the deliberate no-op-push path** (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58): the
  regression pin `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` must
  continue to pass — verification-only items must remain finalisable, now only
  via the explicit signal (per the producer's decision).
- **Lifecycle invariants unchanged**: `StatusLifecycle` remains the only
  writer of status/stage; assignee release on completion is unchanged; the
  terminal read-back assertion (`_assert_terminal_status`) stays as the
  fail-loud guard.
- **Deterministic, machine-checkable gating**: no free-text/heuristic evidence
  parsing as the gate for the no-op path — an explicit flag carries it
  (producer decision Q2).
- **Surgical change**: no new flags or behaviour outside `implement.py finish`
  and `drive`/`phase_parent` classification unless required by the ACs.

## Existing state

- `git_commit` (lines ~2961) returns `True` both when it commits and when the
  tree is clean ("No changes to commit (clean working tree)"), so
  `phase_finish` cannot distinguish a real commit from a no-op.
- After `git_commit`, `phase_finish` reads `git_get_commit_hash(worktree_path)`
  (the branch HEAD — for a clean, commit-less worktree this is the ambient
  `dev` HEAD, i.e. someone else's commit), pushes the identical branch as a
  no-op, and `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes
  `status=completed`/`stage=in_review`. The completion comment reports
  "Implementation complete. Commit: \<ambient HEAD\>".
- `_assert_terminal_status` (lines ~707) only verifies the store *held* the
  terminal write — it cannot distinguish "finished work" from "nothing to do".
- `drive`/`phase_parent` (lines ~9240–9320) run `finish` whenever
  `_has_worktree_changes` is truthy; a clean-but-present worktree is reported
  as "worktree exists … implement, then re-run", but the no-op finish path
  above still finalises a commit-less child when it is reached (observed
  2026-11-01T12:55Z).
- The observed incident: `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1` was flipped
  completed/in_review with zero work; its parent `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` was
  consequently advanced to in_review with AC5 genuinely unmet. Correction was
  applied manually ("Reopened — AC5 measurement was never run (spurious
  finalisation)").

## Desired change

- `git_commit` reports whether a commit was actually created (structured
  result / distinct signal), so `phase_finish` can detect the no-op path
  before the push.
- On the no-op path **without** `--verification-only`: abort before the
  terminal write — item stays open, finish fails loudly with an actionable
  message naming the retained worktree and why, no misattributed commit hash.
- On the no-op path **with** `--verification-only`: finalise as today
  (preserving OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58), but report "no changes / no commit"
  instead of an ambient HEAD.
- `drive`/`phase_parent`: classify a child whose worktree has no attributable
  commit and no verification-only signal as "no work / not finalisable" —
  report and leave open so the parent never advances; keep finish's refusal
  as defence in depth.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_commit` (~2961) commit-vs-no-op
  signal; `git_get_commit_hash` (~3213) attribution; `phase_finish` (~7454)
  refusal + `--verification-only` gating + completion comment wording;
  `_assert_terminal_status` (~707) no-op-path wording; `drive`/`phase_parent`
  (`_classify_child` ~1423, `_has_worktree_changes` ~8798, `_git_path_has_changes`
  ~12099, the drive loop ~9240) classification + reporting.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — existing regression
  pin for the no-op terminal transition; update to assert the gated path and
  add the refusal-path tests.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document `--verification-only` and the no-op
  refusal semantics.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` CLI arg parsing (~12175–12360) — add
  the `--verification-only` flag.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVXU5YWQ004YGZS` — originating work item (this bug, recorded in the llm
  project worklog; moved here because the implement skill source lives in this
  repo).
- `LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1`, `LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM` — the child falsely finalised
  and the parent wrongly advanced to in_review (observed evidence).
- `OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58` — the deliberate no-op-push path for verification-only
  items; its behaviour must be preserved behind the explicit flag.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — regression pin for
  OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58 (terminal status persists on the no-op path).
- Related llm-project items on finish's push/gate correctness (different
  defect surfaces, same file): `LP-0MVTJ2B3H00258U1`, `LP-0MVWY2XQ8005JL0S`,
  `LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0`.
- `SA-0MS8XDUFK004AZ5V` Remove accidentally-tracked .implement_state.json from
  dev — the tracked state file can make a commit-less worktree read as "has
  changes", feeding the false finish; related by find_related.
- `SA-0MVLJXTYY005XQDV` Reconcile terminal child once finish bound exhausted —
  adjacent drive/finish lifecycle reconciliation; related by find_related.
- `SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG` Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull —
  implement-skill maintenance task; related by find_related.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** tightening `finish` could block a legitimate no-op finalise that an
  operator performs directly (without the flag). Mitigation: the refusal
  message names the exact flag/recovery steps, and the manual-push style
  recovery comment mirrors existing finish failure paths.
- **Risk:** `drive` no longer running finish on a "no work" child could strand
  a genuinely complete-but-uncommitted child. Mitigation: the classifier
  checks for dirty files *and* commits ahead (existing `_git_path_has_changes`
  semantics) and reports the child as "not finalisable" with the worktree
  path, so an agent re-enters and finishes it properly.
- **Assumption:** acceptance *evidence* (prose comments citing operational
  runs) is not a machine-checkable gate; the explicit flag is the gate, and
  evidence stays advisory (producer decision Q2).
- **Scope-creep risk:** follow-ups observed during implementation (e.g.
  reconciling `drive` messaging, flag naming) are recorded as separate linked
  work items, not folded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Default outcome of a no-op finish with no commit attributable to the
  item?" — Answer (producer): **(a) Refuse the terminal write** — finish fails
  loudly, item stays open, finalise requires explicit opt-in. Source:
  interactive reply 2026-11-02. **Recommended: (a)**.
- Q2: "What gates legitimate finalisation of a no-commit item
  (verification-only)? (a) explicit CLI flag; (b) recorded acceptance evidence;
  (c) both." — Answer (producer): **(a) explicit CLI flag** (e.g.
  `--verification-only`), no content heuristics. Source: interactive reply
  2026-11-02. **Recommended: (a)**. Research: evidence comments are prose and
  weak as a hard gate; a flag is deterministic and machine-checkable
  (confirmable in `finish`'s report and tests).
- Q3: "drive/phase_parent treatment of a child whose worktree exists but has
  no commit and no finalise signal? (a) classify 'no work / not finalisable' —
  never run finish, keep open so the parent never advances; (b) keep current
  classification, rely on finish's refusal; (c) auto-detect and re-queue."
  — Answer (producer): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-02.
  **Recommended: (a)** — kills the cascade at the source, with finish's own
  refusal as defence in depth for direct invocations.

Research & evidence (agent):
- Traced the no-op path in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `git_commit`
  returns `True` on a clean tree; `git_get_commit_hash` reports the branch HEAD
  (ambient dev HEAD); no-op push; `StatusLifecycle.__exit__` writes the
  terminal transition.
- Read `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py`: the deliberate
  no-op terminal transition is pinned (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58); tests stub
  `git_commit` green and do not distinguish committed vs nothing-to-commit.
- Verified the installed implement skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/`) is a
  byte-identical copy of this repo's `skill/implement/` — this repo is the
  source of truth, hence the item lives here.

- Q4: "How should `drive`/`phase_parent` learn a child is verification-only?"
  (a) recorded in the worktree's `.implement_state.json`
  (`start --verification-only`, and `finish --verification-only` sets it);
  (b) a work-item tag `verification-only` read from `wl show`; (c) both.
  — Answer (producer): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-08.
  **Recommended: (a)** — deterministic, machine-checkable, no store
  mutation, and it matches the `ImplementState` read drive already performs.
  Design consequence (recorded by plan): `ImplementState` gains an optional
  `verification_only` field (default false, tolerant of older state files);
  `phase_finish` treats the state flag OR the `--verification-only` CLI flag
  as the signal.
- Q5: "What shape should the default no-op refusal take?"
  (a) hard failure — non-zero exit, `success: false`, structured
  `steps["commit"]["reason"] = "no_commit_no_signal"`, item left `open`;
  (b) `success: true` with a "not finalised" verdict.
  — Answer (producer): **(a)**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-08.
  **Recommended: (a)** — a false green is exactly the defect; `drive` and
  operators key on the failure.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-08 — Planned by the `plan` skill (this session). Pre-check
  `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium); plan-approval gate
  `request_approval: false` (not Extra Large + High/Severe), so no approval
  pause. Decomposed into four child items in test-first, dependency order:
  SA-0MW74IGEK003IQ2J (task — regression harness, no deps) →
  SA-0MW74IJWI009NRZ1 (feature — finish refusal + `--verification-only`,
  depends on the harness) → SA-0MW74IKJE008JXDQ (feature — drive/phase_parent
  not-finalisable classification, depends on the refusal slice) →
  SA-0MW74IL6B001AMQN (docs — semantics documentation + full-suite verify,
  depends on both feature slices). Producer decisions Q4/Q5 recorded above;
  AC coverage verified by `tree_coverage.apply_coverage_review`.

## Impact

A producer can trust `in_review`: an item whose worktree produced no commit is
no longer silently finalised, so an epic can never be advanced while its
acceptance criteria are still unmet.

# Problem statement

The audit runner's default parent-first flow re-screens gap-mapped children on every parent audit run instead of reusing their content-fresh stored audits, and in `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` mode (default `true`) it overwrites previously serviced child audits with stale `partial` reports — making parent audits loop forever when children have been serviced but the parent still carries gaps.

## Users

- **Producer/Agent**: Runs parent audits on epics with terminal children; expects serviced child audits to persist and the parent to converge.
- **Herdr/Downtime workers**: Automate audits; they hit infinite loops and destroy good audit verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Reuse before re-screen.** In the default parent-first flow (`audit_children=False`), when `parent_gaps` is true and a gap-mapped child has a content-fresh stored audit, the parent reuses the child's persisted AC verdicts and does NOT add the child to `pending_children`.
- **AC2 — Serviced audits are never overwritten.** A parent run must never persist a pending-`partial` child report over a child audit that is content-fresh and carries real (non-pending) verdicts.
- **AC3 — Convergence.** After servicing child screens in-main-slot, a parent re-run reports the single unsatisfiable parent AC only (no `Child screens pending` gate) and clears the `<id>.pending-screens.json` signal.
- **AC4 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover both flows: (a) gap-mapped child reuse skips re-screening, (b) persist does not overwrite a content-fresh serviced child audit. No real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess.

## Impact

Agents running parent audits on epics with serviced children no longer hit infinite re-screen loops or lose their hard-won child audit verdicts — parent audits converge on the first clean pass.

## Constraints

- Must not change the `--audit-children` pre-pass behaviour (it already works correctly).
- In-main-slot mode must remain sequential (no parallelism change).
- Changes must be backwards compatible with existing persisted child audits.

## Existing state

`audit_runner.py::_phase_children` (parent-first `else` branch from ~line 14184; gap-mapped child loop at ~line 14240–14330): when `parent_gaps` is true, the `elif child["id"] in gap_child_ids:` branch (~line 14319) unconditionally appends the child to `pending_children` without checking `_get_child_audit_verdict()` or `_child_content_changed()`. The `--audit-children` pre-pass (same function, `audit_children=True`, ~line 13756) already calls `_get_child_audit_verdict()` and reuses fresh audits. In-main-slot mode then emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens and persists a `partial` child report; a later persist pass overwrites any previously serviced, evidence-backed child audit.

## Desired change

1. **AC1**: In the parent-first gap-mapped path, before adding a child to `pending_children`, consult its stored audit via `_get_child_audit_verdict()` (as the `--audit-children` path does). If content-fresh, adopt the persisted verdicts and skip re-screening.
2. **AC2**: In the persist path for child audits, guard against overwriting a content-fresh child audit. If the target child already has a fresh stored audit with real verdicts, skip persisting the parent-generated pending report.
3. **AC3**: With AC1 + AC2 in place, the `pending-screens.json` signal clears after servicing and the parent converges.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_children` (parent-first gap-mapped child loop ~line 14240–14330; child persist ~line 14438–14475)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_get_child_audit_verdict()` (~line 8182), `_child_content_changed()` (~line 8864)
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — `persist_audit()` (the persistence entry point)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_persist_child_audit()` (~line 7752)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — New/modified tests for gap-mapped reuse and persist-overwrite guards

## Related work

- SA-0MVQJSGLY0098DVB — the epic whose audit exposed this bug (discovered-from)
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45 / SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3 — unserviced in-main-slot handling (mitigates reporting side only)
- LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X — cross-repo consumer AC that makes the parent permanently partial on this host
- SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F — opt-in child audit cascade with run cap (context)
- SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM — related context (find-related)
- SA-0MU32TE120012T49 — related context (find-related)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions — the root cause, evidence, and acceptance criteria are fully specified in the work item description.

# Fix dangling `worktree-isolation.md` link in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`

## Goal

As an agent reading the global instructions at `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, I want
the worktree-isolation reference to open the real SorraAgents document, so I
cannot be sent to a non-existent path mid-run.

## Context

`~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this repository's `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
In the "Implement the work-item" preamble that file links
`[docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md](docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md)`. The target
resolves *inside this checkout*, but a reader whose working reference is
`~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` resolves it to the non-existent
`~/.pi/agent/docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — a dangling link at exactly the
moment an agent is being told it must not write outside a worktree.

The file already uses absolute paths for skill references
(`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md`), so an absolute path to
this repository's document matches the surrounding style and is the
repo-portable reference for a single-user install.

**Cross-repo context (decision recorded 2026-11-02).** Raised as OPEN
QUESTION 1/3 of ContextHub work item `WL-0MVMZLC410001BP9`; the producer chose
to keep the ContextHub item's AC in scope while filing this SorraAgents-scoped
item for the `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` edit (a global-file change cannot ship from a
ContextHub worktree). The producer also chose (Q3, option B) that the global
link targets **this** repository's comprehensive
`docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, while ContextHub's copy gains the
module-resolution section with an explicit cross-link between the two docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Link resolves for the reader.** Reading the installed file
   (`cat ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`), the worktree-isolation reference points at an
   existing absolute path (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`),
   not a bare relative path. Verified by a `grep` of the installed file plus an
   existence check of the target.
2. **No repo-relative-only references remain.** No `](docs/…` or `](skill/…`
   style reference to this repository survives in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`; any
   reference an agent is expected to follow after install uses an absolute path.
3. **Cross-link to the ContextHub doc.** `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
   states what ContextHub's `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` adds beyond it
   (ContextHub-specific guards: main-checkout deletion detection/recovery,
   repo-wide-walk races) and links to that file, so an agent working in
   ContextHub lands on the repo-specific page.
4. **No content regression.** The `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` preamble keeps its
   normative wording (worktree requirement, `cwd`-is-not-sufficient, `wl
   --worklog-dir` guidance); only link targets change.

## Minimal Implementation

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — replace the relative worktree-isolation link with the
  absolute path; sweep the file for other repo-relative links an agent would
  follow after install.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — add the ContextHub cross-link paragraph
  naming what the ContextHub page covers.
- Re-install/verify: `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` symlink unchanged, target exists.

## Constraints

- All changes in an `implement.py` worktree of this repository (no edits from
  the main checkout, no `npm install`/build side effects needed for docs).
- Do not widen scope into the ContextHub doc's module-resolution content — that
  is `WL-0MVMZLC410001BP9`'s work.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVMZLC410001BP9** (ContextHub) — parent intent: document worktree
  module-resolution isolation; its AC2 is satisfied by this item.
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** — link-farm `node_modules` + hard-fail; the
  mechanism ContextHub's new doc section documents. Independent of this item.

# Intake brief — re-filed from OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ (ContentCreator worklog)

**Headline:** Add a consumption mechanism to the refactor skill so that `# <!-- REFACTOR-<id> ... -->` marker blocks are automatically detected as stale and flagged (or removed) when their recorded smell is fixed.

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `# <!-- REFACTOR-<work-item-id> ... -->` blocks into source files to record code smells. The expectation is that whoever fixes the smell also deletes the block. Nothing checks that this happened. Three stale blocks were found in a single sweep, and one live marker remains — proving the gap is ongoing, not a one-off.

## Users

- **Maintainer opening a file.** A stale marker asserts a live smell; disproving it requires a worklog lookup and wastes time.
- **The refactor skill itself (next run).** A stale block reads as a live smell and invites a duplicate work item.
- **The operator running periodic sweeps.** Currently they must manually delete each stale block (OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).

**User story:** "As a developer running the refactor skill or reading a file, I want stale REFACTOR markers to be flagged or removed automatically, so that the tree only contains markers for unfinished work."

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The refactor skill writes markers via `comment_injection.py`; no corresponding consumption code exists.
- Markers contain: `REFACTOR-<id>`, `smell: <type>`, `severity: <level>`, `description: <text>`, and optionally `# status: resolved — <reason>`.
- OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW removed three stale blocks by hand (completed). The consumption gap was recorded as this item (discovered-from:OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).
- One live marker remains in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408) — this is correct and should stay until the smell is fixed.
- The `# status: resolved` line exists in at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) but is not parsed by any tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The refactor skill exposes a reusable function `reap_stale_markers()` (or similar) that scans files for `# <!-- REFACTOR-... -->` blocks and returns a list of stale markers — each entry identifying the file path, line range, work item ID, and the reason the marker is stale (work item terminal / `# status: resolved` present / work item missing).
2. A new CLI entry point `python3 -m skill.refactor.scripts.reap_stale_markers` invokes the function, prints a summary of stale markers found, and exits non-zero if any are discovered — suitable for pre-commit or CI.
3. When invoked with `--dry-run` (default), the tool reports stale markers without modifying files; when invoked with `--remove`, it deletes the marker blocks in-place and preserves all other file content exactly.
4. The function correctly classifies a marker as stale when: (a) the referenced work item's status is `completed` or `deleted` (soft-deleted), or (b) the marker block itself contains `# status: resolved`, or (c) the referenced work item cannot be found (missing or inaccessible) — reason `work-item-missing`. It must NOT flag a marker as stale if the smell is still unfixed (work item is `open` and no resolved line).
5. `python3 -m ruff check` stays clean over all affected files; no `noqa` or config suppression is added.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`./scripts/run_tests.sh`).

## Constraints

- Keep it out of `comment_injection.py` — that mechanism is correct; the gap is consumption.
- The tool must work with the Worklog CLI (`wl show --json`) to check item status; do not add a direct database dependency.
- Do not modify marker copies inside `.worklog/worktrees/*` — only process files in the source tree.
- The `# status: resolved` line format is `# status: resolved — <reason>`; parse this conservatively (presence of `status: resolved` is sufficient).
- If a marker references a work item that cannot be found (item does not exist or is inaccessible), treat it as stale with reason `work-item-missing`.

## Desired change

Add a new module `refactor/reap_markers.py` (or `refactor/consumption.py`) with the detection logic, a CLI entry point, and tests. The refactor skill's main scan should optionally invoke this as a pre-flight or post-flight check.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — reference only; own the marker format, do not modify
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reference only; understand `REFACTOR_PATTERN` matching
- `skill/refactor/reap_markers.py` — new module: detection logic + public API (`reap_stale_markers()`)
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` — new CLI entry point
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the reaper and its place in the scan lifecycle
- `tests/test_refactor/test_reap_markers.py` — new test file (mirrors `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`)

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — Remove stale REFACTOR- marker blocks left in tests and scripts (completed) — manual sweep of three blocks
- `OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L` — Live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py` (ruff C408) — should remain until fixed
- `OSL-0MVM96NMG002ZAMZ` — Recover orphaned refactor-batch edits (completed) — same marker mechanism, different problem
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — Marker-above-shebang near miss (completed) — edge case for comment placement

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the Worklog CLI (`wl show`) is available and reliable for checking item status during the refactor skill's run. **Mitigation:** handle CLI errors gracefully (treat unreachable items as potentially stale with a warning).
- **Risk — false positive:** a marker could reference a completed item that is still relevant as historical context. **Mitigation:** default to `--dry-run` mode; require explicit `--remove` to delete.
- **Risk — scope creep:** turning this into a full repo-wide cleanup sweep. **Mitigation:** scope is the detection/reporting mechanism only; bulk removal is a separate concern.
- **Assumption:** `# status: resolved` is the canonical in-marker resolution signal. **Mitigation:** documented in the new module's docstring; the operator can update if the convention changes.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No interview round was run: the problem, scope, constraints, and related work were answerable by repo and worklog search.

- **Q (resolved by search):** What markers currently exist in the repo? — **Answer:** one live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408, smell still unfixed) and three stale markers that were deleted by OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW. Source: grep, this session.

It is a convention worth formalising in the reap module. Source: `wl show OSL-0MVM4UWDI001GZNY`, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Can the refactor skill invoke `wl`? — **Answer:** yes — the refactor skill's scripts already use the Worklog CLI (e.g., `wl list --tags Refactor`). Source: inspection of `comment_injection.py`, `workitem_creation.py`, this session.
- **Duplicate check:** `wl search "REFACTOR marker reap consumption stale"` returned only OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ itself and OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW (the manual sweep). No item covers automated consumption.

## Appendix: plan-session questions (plan skill)

Planning stopped at the interview step: the item cannot be decomposed into
implementation tasks until repository ownership is settled.

- **OPEN QUESTION (blocking; directed to the producer):** Which repository

  - **Preferred option: (a).**

## Goal

`docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.7 documents the **Python** hermetic
git-environment helpers (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`:
`run_git`/`fixture_git_env`/`git_env_for_repo`, plus the `IndexWatch` guard),
but not their **JavaScript** counterpart that the same fix introduced. An
audit of SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX judged its AC2 ("all related documentation is
updated to reflect the changes") unmet for exactly this reason:

> `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.7 covers the fixture rule generally but does
> not name the new JS module `skill/shared/git_env.mjs` or `hermeticGitEnv`.

## Evidence

| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| JS production helpers | `skill/shared/git_env.mjs` — `hermeticGitEnv()`, `gitEnvForRepo()`, `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_VARS`, `INDEX_ENV_VAR` |
| Test re-export | `tests/helpers/hermeticGitEnv.mjs` |
| Unit coverage | `tests/unit/test-hermeticGitEnv.mjs` (heredity, override scrub, index drop, pass-through) |
| Consumers | `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-worklog-ref-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-python-project-release-bump.mjs`, `skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` (`gitEnvForRepo`) |
| Doc gap | `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.7 — no mention of `git_env.mjs`, `hermeticGitEnv` or `gitEnvForRepo` |

## Required documentation

- Add a "JavaScript counterpart" subsection to §9.7 that names
  `skill/shared/git_env.mjs` and the rule: **node test fixtures** route git
  through `hermeticGitEnv()` (via `tests/helpers/hermeticGitEnv.mjs`), and
  **production scripts that inspect a named repository** use `gitEnvForRepo(repo)`
  (which keeps an ambient `GIT_INDEX_FILE` only when it lies inside that
  repository's git directory).
- State explicitly that the `IndexWatch` per-test guard in the same section is
  a **pytest** autouse fixture and therefore Python-only — node suites rely on
  the helper rule, not on the guard.
- Cross-reference the unit coverage so a reader can see the contract is pinned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — JS rule documented.** `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.7 names
  `skill/shared/git_env.mjs`, `hermeticGitEnv()` and `gitEnvForRepo()`, and
  states the fixture vs production distinction consistently with the module
  docstring.
- **AC2 — Guard scope stated.** The section states that the `IndexWatch` guard
  is Python-only and that node suites depend on the helper rule instead.
- **AC3 — Coverage referenced.** The documented contract is traceable to
  `tests/unit/test-hermeticGitEnv.mjs` (and the node consumers), and no
  existing §9.7 statement becomes inaccurate.
- **AC4 — UK English, valid cross-references** (relative links resolve).

## Out of scope

- Any behaviour change to `git_env.mjs` or the node suites.
- Re-documenting the Python helpers already covered by §9.7.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-18)

**Decision: no child decomposition.** This is a single-file documentation edit
(one subsection plus one clarifying sentence in the same section). Splitting it
into child items would put concurrent worktrees on the same lines of
`docs/dev/test-isolation.md` for no benefit, so the plan is recorded here as an
actionable implementation sketch instead.

**Scope boundary (documented assumption).** Only `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
§9.7 changes. `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (the authoritative
node-test authoring guidance) is **not** touched: naming the helper there would
be useful, but AC1–AC4 and the item's Out-of-scope section do not ask for it, so
it is left as a follow-on candidate rather than an invented requirement.

### Ordered implementation steps

1. **Add `#### JavaScript counterpart` to §9.7**, between the existing
   `#### The rule` bullet list (Python helpers) and `#### The guard`:
   - name `skill/shared/git_env.mjs` as the JS counterpart of
     `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, exporting `hermeticGitEnv()`,
     `gitEnvForRepo()`, `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_VARS` and `INDEX_ENV_VAR`;
   - **fixture rule:** node test fixtures spawn git with

     `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs`), mirroring the Python
     “explicit value wins” note in the existing rule.
2. **Scope the `IndexWatch` guard sentence.** In `#### The guard`, state that
   the guard is a **pytest** autouse fixture armed by the repo-root
   `conftest.py` (`skill/shared/inherited_index_guard.py`), so it is
   **Python-only**; node suites have no equivalent guard and rely on the helper
   rule in step 1. Keep every existing `IndexWatch` statement intact.
3. **Cross-reference coverage** in the new subsection:
   `tests/unit/test-hermeticGitEnv.mjs` (override scrubbing, index drop,
   copy-never-mutate, caller-layered overrides) plus the node consumers
   `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-worklog-ref-gate.mjs`,
   `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs`,
   `tests/unit/test-python-project-release-bump.mjs` and
   `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs`.
4. **Consistency read-through of §9.7.** The existing example
   “Fixture git commands use the hermetic helpers” is Python (`run_git`
   / `fixture_git_env`); keep it and label it as the Python form so it does not
   read as the only supported route. Flag anything else that the new text would
   contradict.
5. **Verify.** Relative links resolve from `docs/dev/`
   (`../../skill/shared/git_env.mjs`,
   `../../tests/unit/test-hermeticGitEnv.mjs`), UK English throughout, and no
   existing §9.7 statement is invalidated. Docs-only change: the changed-scope

### Acceptance-criteria mapping

|----|-----------------|
| AC1 — JS rule documented (module, `hermeticGitEnv`, `gitEnvForRepo`, fixture vs production) | 1 |
| AC2 — guard scope stated (Python-only; node relies on helper rule) | 2 |
| AC3 — coverage referenced, no stale §9.7 statement | 3 + 4 |
| AC4 — UK English, resolving relative links | 5 |

### Verification / definition of done

- `grep -n "git_env.mjs\|hermeticGitEnv\|gitEnvForRepo" docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
  returns the new subsection (AC1), and the guard paragraph names
  `IndexWatch` as pytest-only (AC2).

## Problem statement

During `implement.py finish`, the refactor step detects pre-existing code smells and attempts to file a worklog work item for each. When work item creation is skipped (a guard hit: ephemeral worktree, file not found, duplicate REFACTOR comment, existing worklog item, audit twin) or fails (`wl create` error), `remediate_pre_existing()` silently drops the finding — it increments `comment_errors` and logs only a generic `"No work item ID for smell … skipping comment"` warning. Neither the guard that fired nor the failure reason reaches the finish report, so the framework's own lint debt accumulates invisibly: the observed run showed `pre_existing: 5`, `work_items_created: 0`, `comment_errors: 5` with no explanation of *why* every smell was dropped.

## Users

- **Producers** reviewing a finish report who need to know whether pre-existing lint debt is tracked or was silently dropped.
- **Agents** running `implement.py finish` that rely on the report to prove a clean gate rather than an unexamined one.

Example user story: *As a producer reviewing a finish report, I want every detected pre-existing smell to show either the work item that tracks it or the specific reason it was skipped, so I can trust that framework lint debt is not accumulating invisibly.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Every skipped pre-existing smell records its skip reason.** When `create_smell_work_item()` returns `None`, the refactor step records which guard fired (ephemeral `.worklog/worktrees` target, missing source file, existing REFACTOR comment, existing worklog item, audit-family twin, or `wl create` failure) for that specific smell.
2. **The finish report carries a per-smell remediation breakdown.** The refactor report's `remediation` section includes, for every pre-existing smell, its identity (smell type, code, repository-relative file) and either the created work-item ID (plus REFACTOR comment outcome) or the recorded skip reason — so `comment_errors: 5` is never the only signal.
3. **Findings are never silently lost.** For every detected pre-existing smell the report shows exactly one outcome — tracked (work item + comment) or explicitly explained-skipped — and the counts reconcile (`pre_existing == tracked + explained_skipped`). No smell is dropped without a recorded reason in the report.
4. **The finish gate surfaces the breakdown.** `implement.py finish` output (via `run_refactor()` → report) includes the per-smell remediation outcome so a producer sees the reason without reading raw refactor subprocess logs.
5. **Re-running `implement.py finish` on the same tree produces identical remediation outcomes** (idempotent — no duplicate work items, no duplicate report entries).
6. **Automated tests cover each skip reason** — a test per guard/failure path (ephemeral worktree, missing file, duplicate REFACTOR comment, existing worklog item, audit twin, `wl create` failure) asserting the reason reaches the report, plus a reconciliation test (`pre_existing == tracked + explained_skipped`).
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Producers and agents can see exactly why each pre-existing smell finding was not tracked, so framework lint debt can no longer accumulate invisibly.

## Constraints

- Changes are confined to the refactor skill (`skill/refactor/`) and the reporting surface in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`run_refactor()` / finish report assembly).
- Must not change smell *detection* logic or work-item *creation* decision logic — only make existing decisions observable in the report.
- Must not add new external dependencies; reuse existing logging/report structures.
- Must preserve existing dedupe behaviour (same-identity grouping, existing-item reuse, audit-twin suppression) — those remain correct guards; only their outcome must become visible.

## Existing state

`remediate_pre_existing()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` calls `create_smell_work_items_mapped()` then iterates smells to inject REFACTOR comments. `create_smell_work_item()` in `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` returns `None` from several guards, each logging only a `LOG.warning`/`LOG.info` line. When the mapped ID is `None`, `remediate_pre_existing()` increments `comment_errors` and logs a single generic warning. `run_refactor()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` captures the refactor subprocess stdout as the report, so the finish report shows only `{"comment_errors": N}` with no per-smell breakdown.

## Desired change

Make the skip/track decision per smell observable in the refactor report:
- Introduce a structured per-smell outcome record (identity + `created` with item ID + comment status, or `skipped` with a reason enum) produced by the remediation pass and returned in the report's `remediation` section.
- Have `remediate_pre_existing()` collect these outcomes instead of only counting `comment_errors`, while keeping the existing guards unchanged.
- Ensure `run_refactor()` propagates the enriched remediation data into the finish report so `implement.py finish` shows the reasons.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `remediate_pre_existing()` must record structured per-smell outcomes (created vs skipped + reason) instead of only incrementing `comment_errors`.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — `create_smell_work_item()` guards must surface *which* guard fired (return-with-reason or a parallel outcome map), without changing the guards' decisions.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_refactor()` must propagate the enriched remediation breakdown into the finish report.
- `tests/test_refactor/` and `skill/implement/tests/` — new/updated tests covering each skip reason and the report breakdown.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW7Z1AU1006UT9C** (completed): Refactor dedupe — substring matching caused the same smell to be filed repeatedly.
- **SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG**: Same-identity grouping so each identity maps to a single work item (identity→item mapping used by comment injection).
- **SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO**: Audit-family twin suppression (`ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` chores).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB** – Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill release process (completed)
- **SA-0MQA71IRS002KU2O** – Code Comment Injection Module (completed)
- **SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4** – Implement: unified parser and remove_refactor_marker() (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, accumulate, analyzed, auto, ble001 (+80 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvze164p0048306, acceptance, accumulate, auto, ble001 (+77 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvze164p0048306, acceptance, auto, blind, blocking (+72 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the seed context (source log excerpt, the reported `remediation` JSON, and the identified call chain `remediate_pre_existing()` → `create_smell_work_items_mapped()` → `create_smell_work_item()`) already defined the problem and desired outcome. Requirements were derived from repository inspection.

- Q: "Does a pre-existing smell already create a work item on the happy path?" — Answer (research, agent): Yes — `create_smell_work_item()` creates an item and `remediate_pre_existing()` injects a REFACTOR comment when `created_map[finding_key]` is set. Source: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` lines ~443–477; `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` `create_smell_work_item()`.
- Q: "Which branch drops the finding without a report reason?" — Answer (research, agent): The `if not smell_work_item_id:` branch in `remediate_pre_existing()` (generic warning + `comment_errors += 1`), reached whenever `create_smell_work_item()` returns `None` from any guard or a `wl create` failure. Source: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` lines ~458–464.
- Q: "Are the recorded smells session-introduced or pre-existing?" — Answer (source log, SA-0MVZE164P0048306 finish log): pre-existing (`session_introduced: 0`, `pre_existing: 5`); the item that surfaced this landed green. Source: `/tmp/finish2_SA-0MVZE164P0048306.log`.

`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (added in v0.1.25) builds a fixture release repo and drives `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` with a stubbed suite runner. Under a clean shell the module is green (verified: `run_tests.py --scope full --force` at tree a9b008ead → 5820 passed). Under the **pre-push hook** (i.e. any push to `dev`/`main`) the same three tests fail:

```
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestGreenGate::test_green_gate_invokes_full_scope_and_release_proceeds
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestRedGate::test_red_gate_blocks_release_before_pr
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestMissingRunnerFailClosed::test_missing_runner_fails_closed
FileNotFoundError: .../runner-marker.txt   (the stubbed runner was never invoked)
```

Root cause: git exports `GIT_DIR` (and the suite gate may export `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) into hook environments; the fixture repo's git commands then resolve against the *live* checkout instead of the fixture, so `merge-dev-to-main.sh` short-circuits and the suite gate never runs. This is the same class as SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX (node fixtures inheriting the finish gate's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`).

**Consequence:** the pre-push full-suite gate is red for every `dev` push, so `dev` cannot be synced with `main` after a release (hit during the 2026-11-02 v0.1.25 release; the sync required `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` with a separately verified green tree).

## Impact

Users can now push `dev` after a release without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, enabling automated `dev`→`main` promotion to complete without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` scrubs the ambient git environment (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or equivalent) for both the fixture repo construction and the merge-script subprocess, so it passes when run from a git hook.
2. A regression test proves the module passes with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the live repository.
3. `git push origin dev` (fast-forward) succeeds without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` after the fix.
4. Full suite green in both a clean shell and a hook-like environment.

## Related

- SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX — same leak class for node fixtures.
- SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42 — audit/producer-review churn (unrelated, same release session).

# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>   (historical reproduction in a sibling project)
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no
  `skill/` tree, so a TCE `implement.py` worktree could not carry the change
  (the TCE-side `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits).
  Options were: (a) transfer the item to the SA store; (b) create an SA item
  carrying code + tests, keep the CG item as a linked discovery record;
  (c) commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a worktree (breaks
  worktree-isolation). Agent recommendation: (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"SA create there then delete this item"* — create the
  SA item with the full brief (this item) **and delete** the CG item, i.e. a
  transfer rather than a linked pair. Source: operator reply in the intake
  session `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q2 — Fold in the adjacent `code_freeze.py` defect?** Options: (a) fix both
  in this change via one shared helper; (b) keep this item narrow and file the
  `code_freeze` fix as a separate `discovered-from` item. Agent recommendation:
  (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — the `code_freeze.py`
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` duplicate-walk fix is filed as its own item; this item
  stays narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q3 — Duplicate-work check (agent-resolved).** Searched both stores
  (`worklog_dir_flag`, `worktree resolution`, `nested worklog dir`) —
  `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` is the only overlapping item and its ACs do not cover
  the nesting/initialisation defects, so no duplicate close or rewrite was
  applied; it is cross-referenced in *Related work*. Answer: **no full
  duplicate; partial overlap cross-linked.**
## Impact

Skill scripts that shell out to `wl` (render_report, persist_audit, audit, status/lifecycle helpers) now resolve the main checkout's initialised worklog store correctly from any `implement.py` worktree cwd — `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…`, its subdirectories, or a plain nested project — so an agent reporting or transitioning status from a worktree always targets the store the producer reads, with no manual `--worklog-dir` correction and no "Worklog system is not initialized" failure or `.worklog/.worklog` mis-targeting.

# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the freeze semantics: this is a path-resolution fix, not a
  change to how a freeze is activated, cleared, or enforced.
- Keep the existing public API (`code_freeze_marker_path`, marker read/write
  helpers) and their `project_root` behaviour unchanged.
- Prefer re-using the shared helper over a second walk; if that would create a
  circular import, mirror the rule and reference the canonical one in a
  comment.
- Gate order: build → test → commit; no ad-hoc `pytest` — run tests through the
  test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake of the parent item)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 48) order:
  explicit `project_root` → `<cwd>/.worklog` → `<git toplevel>/.worklog` →
  `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`, each gated on `is_dir()` only.
- `code_freeze_marker_path()` (~line 90) uses that helper and falls back to
  `<cwd>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` when nothing resolves.
- The same candidate-construction defect is proven in
  `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` (parent item
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB`, AC1–AC3) — this item is the same rule applied to the
  code-freeze copy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` / marker path
  resolution (~lines 48–101).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` — new worktree-layout cases
  (AC1–AC3).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — one sentence alongside the
  `StatusLifecycle` resolution note (if the rule is shared).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the shared helper is exported
  for reuse (no behaviour change expected here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` — parent fix for `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()`
  / `worklog_dir_flag()` (same rule, `wl`-facing seam). This item should land
  after it so the shared rule exists.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`, `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine) —
  discovery chain for the original defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: freeze bypass stays latent** until this item is implemented, if the
  parent fix lands alone. Mitigation: the parent item's docs state the
  code-freeze copy is still defective and link here.
- **Risk: duplicated rule drifts again.** Mitigation: AC4 prefers the shared
  helper.
- **Scope-creep risk:** touching freeze activation/enforcement or adding new
  marker features — out of scope; record such ideas as separate items.
- **Assumption:** the implement workflow's freeze check is the only consumer of
  `code_freeze_marker_path()`; verified by grep during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Fold this into the parent `worklog_dir_flag` fix?**
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — filed here; the parent item stays
  narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`, relayed via
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (Appendix Q2).

data.description:
# Reduce Large Tool-Call Results Before They Enter Conversation History

## Problem Statement

A single oversized tool-call result (e.g. a 51 KB SKILL.md pasted by the audit skill) inflates the conversation history, causing every subsequent model turn to re-prefill a bloated tail. Measured impact: a 51,945-byte tool message inflated 6,564 to 33,570 tokens across 7 turns, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill. The proxy under-priced the append (173 tokens billed vs. 12,936 measured), making the cost invisible to admission control.

## Users

- **Pi agents**: All agents working with tool results that exceed reasonable sizes (skill bodies, large file reads, JSON dumps) will benefit from automatic result reduction.
- **Operators**: Reduced prefill times mean faster response cycles and lower GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1), is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.

## Impact

Agents experience faster response times when working with tool results, as oversized payloads are automatically reduced before entering conversation history, avoiding 50+ second prefill delays on subsequent turns.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. A ~2 s small-model call must avoid 45-90 s of prefill (saving ~13k tokens at 143-303 tok/s).
- Any lossy step must be recoverable — raw payload retained and re-readable via `offset`/`limit` parameters.
- Runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects; competes for capacity, hence the preference for non-model approaches first.
- Must not alter the tool-call contract — agents must still be able to read content they couldn't fit in one call.

## Candidate Approaches (cheapest first)

1. **Measure first** — rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions (deterministic script, no model calls).
2. **Truncate with re-read** — Pi extension intercepts oversized tool results, keeps head/tail, preserves raw output on disk with a re-read marker.
3. **Reference instead of inline** — content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files), substitute a short handle plus preview.
4. **Small-model compaction** — detect oversized tool results, ask a small model (Qwen2.5-7B summariser slot) to compact them. Escalate only when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient.
5. **Structured projections** — JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, at the tool level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `command/pi.mjs` or equivalent — where tool-call results enter the conversation
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` or audit skill scripts — source of one measured oversized payload
- `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` — session recordings for measurement analysis
- `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` — session jsonl files for measurement analysis
- Pi extension framework files — for the truncation/reference implementation

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Five candidate approaches could tempt implementing all of them. Risk: scope expansion. Mitigation: implement one non-model mechanism for AC3; assess all five for AC2; defer small-model compaction unless validated as necessary.
- **Threshold selection**: The truncation threshold (AC3) must be chosen carefully — too aggressive loses useful content, too permissive doesn't solve the problem. Risk: wrong default. Mitigation: measurement report (AC1) informs threshold; make it configurable.
- **Agent confusion**: Agents may not understand truncation markers or how to re-read content. Risk: agent errors. Mitigation: clear documentation (AC5); test with real agent sessions.
- **GPU contention**: Approach 4 (small-model compaction) competes for the same GPU. Risk: compaction takes longer than prefill savings. Mitigation: benchmark against prefill cost (AC4); fallback to no-op when summariser unavailable.
- **Assumption**: Session recordings at `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` and `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` are available for measurement analysis. If not accessible, the measurement script (AC1) should gracefully handle this.

## Related Work

- Originating evidence: LLM-repo worklog items LP-0MW0KZUUS002LICZ (prefill pricing) and LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI.
- Session recordings at `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` and session jsonl files at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should this work be implemented in the SorraAgents repo or the LLM proxy repo? — Answer (agent@herdr): The Pi extension prototype should live in SorraAgents (where Pi extensions are managed), but the measurement script and documentation should link back to the LLM-repo prefill-pricing items. Source: intake assessment.
- Q: What threshold should trigger truncation? — Answer (agent@herdr): TBD — the measurement report (AC1) will inform a data-driven threshold. A reasonable starting point for prototyping is 10 KB or ~5,000 tokens. Source: intake assessment, to be confirmed by measurement.
- Q: Should the extension handle both text and binary results? — Answer (agent@herdr): Focus on text-based results (file reads, tool output) for AC3; binary handling can be deferred to implementation. Source: intake assessment.
