# Refactor skill injects finding comments into whatever checkout it runs in

## Problem

Discovered during intake of SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly
to `dev` in the main checkout).

The refactor skill writes `<!-- REFACTOR-<item-id> -->` markers directly into
source files in its current working directory. When a downtime-dispatched session
runs it with `--cwd <main checkout root>`, it dirties the shared main checkout
without committing anything.

Observed 2026-11-18 ~16:08-16:12 during a concurrent refactor session: the main
checkout was dirtied with `<!-- REFACTOR-SA-… -->` injections in
`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py` and
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` (plus
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

This is a **second main-checkout mutation surface** distinct from the
direct-commit path tracked in SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU: refactor does not commit, but
a dirty checkout `gate-refused` a concurrent pre-push (the same class of damage —
it blocks other sessions' pushes and worktree creation).

## Relation to the parent item

- Parent SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU covers **commits** on `dev` in the main checkout
  (skill commit helpers, the `.githooks/pre-commit` guard, `start` attribution,
  `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh`).
- This item covers **uncommitted writes** by the refactor skill. Its commit-time
  guard does not fire (no commit is made), so it needs its own fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refactor skill refuses to inject finding comments when its target root is
  the main checkout (detected as `git rev-parse --git-dir` ==
  `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, the same rule as the pre-commit guard), and
  reports an actionable message pointing at the worktree requirement.
- Existing behaviour is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch.
- A `git_sandbox` test pins both the refusal (main checkout unchanged, no
  markers written) and the worktree/feature-branch success path.
- Documentation states that refactor must run in a worktree, cross-referencing
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Impact

A dispatched refactor session can no longer dirty the shared main checkout,
which today blocks concurrent pre-push gates and worktree creation.

## Plan

Decomposed into five child work items, test-first and dependency-ordered:

| # | Work item | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test: shared is_main_checkout() unit tests | Pin the main-checkout detection rule (`git rev-parse --git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`) |
| 2 | Implement: shared is_main_checkout() helper | One shared predicate in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` next to `main_checkout_root()` |
| 3 | Test: refactor main-checkout refusal and worktree success | `git_sandbox` tests pinning the refusal **and** the preserved worktree/feature-branch path |
| 4 | Implement: refactor main-checkout write refusal | Pipeline pre-flight guard + injection-level defence in depth |
| 5 | Docs: refactor must run in a worktree | `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` plus `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` |

Dependency chain: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 (each implementation item depends on the test
item that pins it).

### Design decisions

- **One detection rule, one implementation.** The guard reuses the
  pre-commit/pre-push rule and is exposed once as
  `git_sandbox.is_main_checkout(path)`; the refactor skill does not re-implement
  git plumbing.
- **Fail fast, before any write.** The guard runs at the start of
  `refactor_pipeline`, before linter auto-fix (ruff/eslint `--fix` also write
  files in place) and before work-item creation. The refusal test can only
  assert "main checkout unchanged" if auto-fix is prevented too.
- **Defence in depth.** `inject_refactor_comment()` also refuses when the target
  file's repository root is the main checkout, so a caller that bypasses the
  pipeline still cannot mark files.
- **`--dry-run` is exempt** — it writes nothing, and read-only inspection of
  the main checkout stays possible.
- **Not in a git work tree → never refuse** (predicate returns `False`), so the
  skill keeps working outside git.
- **Vertical slice note:** effort is Small, so the change is phased as
  test→implementation pairs (shared helper, then refactor behaviour) followed by
  docs; each phase is independently landable and gated by its preceding test
  item. No horizontal layering.

### Effort and risk

Small effort (O=3h, M=6h, P=12h → 6.5h expected, 10.5h with overheads), Medium
risk (7/25; main driver is a false-positive refusal breaking legitimate runs,
mitigated by delegating to the existing git-plumbing rule, exempting
`--dry-run`, and testing the worktree success path).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18: Initial decomposition (5 children in a test-first dependency
  chain), effort/risk estimated, AC coverage review at 100% (`proceed`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Seed context: bug item, priority medium, stage `intake_complete` at planning
start, no children, no prior Appendix entries. Discovered during intake of
SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly to `dev` in the main
checkout); related, non-overlapping items reviewed: SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG
(marker identity, completed), SA-0MVXVBYXI000QMXM and SA-0MVXVC127009T0NP
(pre-push guard failure paths, completed), SA-0MW5KKEHL005BR0L (marker
cross-wiring, open). No existing or completed item covers this refusal.

**Producer interview:** none required — the acceptance criteria already pin the
detection rule, the refusal behaviour, the test requirement and the
documentation requirement. Duplicate-work check performed; no overlapping
completed item found.

**OPEN QUESTION (to: producer, non-blocking)** — AC2 reads "Existing behaviour
is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch." Under the stated
detection rule, a feature branch checked out **in the main checkout** is still
the main checkout (`git-dir` == `git-common-dir`) and would therefore be
refused. The plan assumes "feature branch" means the normal agent flow — a
feature branch inside a linked worktree created by `implement.py start` — and
preserves that path. Why it matters: the alternative reading (allow the main
checkout when the branch is not `dev`) needs a different detection rule than
the one AC1 prescribes. Assumption adopted; nothing is blocked.

**Decision (agent, from the item text)** — the refusal is fail-fast at pipeline
start rather than a per-injection skip, because AC3 requires the refusal test to
assert "main checkout unchanged", which is only true when auto-fix writes are
prevented as well as marker injection.

**Decision (agent)** — the predicate lives in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
beside `main_checkout_root()`/`is_worktree_git_dir()` so the commit-helper
guard items (SA-0MWMCVFXB0096UG5, SA-0MWMCVNK0003QVW8) reuse one rule instead
of growing a third copy.

**Observed at planning time (evidence, not a work item)** — the main checkout
was dirty with exactly the described artefacts (`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`,
`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`,
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py`,
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), a live reproduction by a concurrent
dispatched refactor session. The planning session made no changes to those
files.
data.title: Refactor skill injects finding comments into the main checkout

# Ruff ISC004 in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py:715` — candidate false positive (producer decision)

## Problem statement

The audit's ruff screen reports `ISC004` ("Unparenthesized implicit string
concatenation in collection") at `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py:715-716` and
`:717-721`. Both are deliberate multi-part f-strings that form single
`render_summary()` list entries, with the separating comma present as the
list-element separator — a candidate false positive. Whether to accept it once
via an audit waiver or to make the intent explicit in code is a producer
decision, and the same decision is already open on the sibling chores
SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI (line 712) and SA-0MWMOCFHU007PLOZ (line 717).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — takes each candidate-false-positive decision once,
  so the finding stops re-entering the producer-review queue.
- **Auditors and the automated review pipeline** — currently re-file the same
  accepted sites as new medium/low chores after unrelated edits.
- **Maintainers of `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`** — the summary rendering must
  keep producing byte-identical output.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want one decision on `ISC004` in this file, so the same
  already-accepted finding stops coming back after a five-line edit elsewhere.
- As a maintainer, I want the summary code to state its intent so a reader
  cannot mistake the deliberate concatenation for a forgotten comma.
- As an auditor, I want a resolution that does **not** silence `ISC004` for the
  whole file if a genuine missing comma could hide there.

## Evidence gathered

- **Reproduction:** `ruff check --isolated --select ISC004
  scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` (ruff 0.16.0) → exactly 2 findings, at
  `715:9` and `717:9`. Ruff's own help for both: *"Did you forget a comma?" /
  "Wrap implicitly concatenated strings in parentheses"*.
- **Not a general style complaint:** lines 700-708 (`render_checks`)
  concatenate in exactly the same way but are **not** flagged, because they sit
  inside parenthesised `lines.append(...)` calls — `ISC004` only fires on
  unparenthesised concatenation inside a collection literal.
- **The concatenation is intentional:** the `window:` pair and the five-part
  `corpus:` group each render one human-readable summary line; the trailing
  comma on `716`/`721` is the list-element separator, not a missing comma.
- **Why the same sites keep re-appearing (line drift):** the previously filed
  chores for this file covered these same two constructs
  (SA-0MWB1AYW0003DKQR line 710 — waived and closed; SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI line
  712 — decision pending). An **uncommitted** 5-line refactor marker added at the
  top of the file (`git diff` shows the `REFACTOR-SA-0MWMBFHYN005STJV`
  formatting marker, 5 insertions) shifted both constructs by +5 lines, so the
  line-specific waiver on 710 no longer matches and the audit re-filed the same
  code as 715/717.
- **Waiver matching semantics** (`audit_runner._matching_waiver`): a waiver
  **without** `--line` accepts the rule for the whole file and survives line

  finding stops generating chores and review-queue entries.

because the intentional multi-line string split is now explicitly parenthesised

## Summary

Wrap the two multi-line f-string entries in `render_summary()`'s `lines` list in explicit parentheses, resolving both ruff ISC004 sites in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`. This is the producer-chosen Option A (fix in code) from the parent brief.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both live `ISC004` sites in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` (`715-716` and `717-721`) are resolved so `ruff check --isolated --select ISC004 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` reports zero findings for the file.
2. The resolution survives line drift: the code no longer triggers the ISC004 rule, so no audit waiver is needed and no new ISC004 chore will be filed for this file after unrelated edits.
3. Rendered output is unchanged: the existing `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` tests for `render_summary()` pass unchanged, and at least one focused assertion covers the parenthesised form.
4. Sibling chores for the same two constructs (SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI line 712, SA-0MWMOCFHU007PLOZ line 717) are cross-referenced and closed or superseded by this resolution — no duplicate work is performed.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant docs entries.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Implementation

In `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, the `render_summary()` function builds a `lines = [...]` list. The first two entries (the `window:` pair at lines 715-716 and the `corpus:` group at lines 717-721) use implicit string concatenation without surrounding parentheses.

**Change:** wrap each multi-line f-string entry in parentheses, matching the pattern already used in `render_checks()` (lines 700-708).

```python
# Before:
lines = [
    f"window: {report['window_start']} .. {report['window_end']} "
    f"(since post-fix {report['post_fix_commit']})",
    f"corpus: root={report['sessions_root']} "
    f"files_scanned={report['files_scanned']} "
    f"files_with_samples={report['files_with_samples']} "
    f"records_in_window={report['records_in_window']} "
    f"samples={report['total_samples']}",
]

# After:
lines = [
    (f"window: {report['window_start']} .. {report['window_end']} "
     f"(since post-fix {report['post_fix_commit']})"),
    (f"corpus: root={report['sessions_root']} "
     f"files_scanned={report['files_scanned']} "
     f"files_with_samples={report['files_with_samples']} "
     f"records_in_window={report['records_in_window']} "
     f"samples={report['total_samples']}"),
]
```

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — lines 715-721: wrap both list entries in parentheses.

data.description:
## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` builds once (Step 2), then pushes to `dev`. When the push
loses a race and is rejected non-fast-forward, `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
fetches `origin/dev`, rebases the feature branch, recomputes the commit hash
and retries the push — **without rebuilding the worktree**. The pre-push hook
then runs the full suite against the rebased tree, where `packages/shared/dist`
(gitignored, produced by the build) is stale with respect to the `dev` commits
the rebase just pulled in. The gate goes red for a condition that does not
exist in a built tree, and the item's work is stranded until a human rebuilds.

## Users

- **Dispatch agent (leaf `finish` / driven child)** — "When my push loses a
  race to a sibling push, I want the retry to gate a tree I actually built, so
  my item lands instead of failing on a `TypeError` that names a function my
  own change set never touched."
- **Producer / operator on duty** — "I want a red dev-push gate to always mean
  something real about the pushed change set, so I never spend an hour and a
  half hand-rebuilding a worktree to clear a false red."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a successful recovery rebase inside the push loop, `finish` builds the
   rebased worktree **before** the retry push reaches the full-suite gate. A
   test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose rebase introduces a new
   `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and
   the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
2. A stale-dist failure is never attributed to the item's own change set. A
   test asserts that a gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build
   (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` — a runtime error that the
   existing load-flake retry does not match) cannot be reported as a failure of
   the pushed change set: either the run rebuilds first, or it fails closed with
   a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
3. A genuine red introduced by the rebased commit is still reported red. A test
   pins that the rebuild does not weaken the gate: when the rebased tree really
   fails the suite, the push is blocked and the item stays `open`.
4. `finish` on a worktree whose push is rejected once still lands the commit and
   writes the terminal `completed` / `in_review` transition (no manual
   intervention).
5. A rebuild that itself fails after the rebase fails **closed**: no push, an
   actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the item is
   reset to `open` (mirroring the existing Step 2 build-failure path) — an
   unbuilt tree is never gated.
6. No extra build is paid when no rebase happened: the normal (uncontended) push
   path keeps exactly one build per `finish`, and the changed-scope gate
   (Step 3) is never re-entered by the retry loop.
7. Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and
   pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no
   vacuous green).
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A dispatch whose push races another push lands its work instead of spending an
hour and a half chasing a build-staleness false-red.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single build entry point `run_build(cwd)` so the rebuild
  inherits the current behaviour (disk-backed `TMPDIR` injection, 300 s timeout,
  no-build-script no-op for Python-only repos) — no parallel build code path.
- The rebuild runs **inside** the push retry loop, after the rebase and before
  the retry `git_push_to_dev` call; the Step 3 changed-scope gate and the
  "at most one full-suite gate per finish" property (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) must
  survive.
- Never weaken the gate: a reproducible red on the rebuilt tree still blocks the
  push.
- Stay within the module's existing retry budget semantics
  (`DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`): a rebuild failure is a hard stop, not a
  retryable transport condition.
- Worktree-only changes; no behaviour change for the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:12262`)
  does: fetch `origin/dev` → `git rebase origin/dev` → capture the rewritten
  hash → `_assert_push_subject` → retry `git_push_to_dev`. There is no build
  step anywhere on this path.
- `run_build` (`implement.py:9324`) is the single build entry point; `phase_finish`
  Step 2 calls it once before tests (`implement.py:12763`).
- The pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs the full suite for `dev` pushes,
  bound to the pushed commit via `run_tests.py --gate-commit`, resolved by
  `resolve_gate_subject` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:3697`) — normally the
  worktree in place ("cheap in-place run"), so the suite executes against the
  worktree's filesystem including its `packages/shared/dist`.
- The verdict is tree-keyed (SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG) with change-set reuse
  (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC): a pure rebase is usually served from the pre-race
  verdict, so no suite runs. When the change set fingerprint **also** differs —
  e.g. the concurrently landed commit edited the same hub file the item edited
  (`packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` in the observed case) — the key misses,
  the suite really runs, and it runs on stale `dist`.
- Existing mitigation `_is_gate_load_flake` (`implement.py:6032`) retries once on
  suite *load* errors (`Cannot find package`, `Cannot find module`,
  `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). A stale-dist runtime `TypeError` **loads fine** and falls
  outside those patterns, and retrying the identical unbuilt tree could not help
  anyway.
- `packages/shared/dist` is gitignored and produced by `npm run build`, so it is
  invisible to the tree fingerprint: two trees with identical git content can
  carry different `dist` contents. That is precisely the mismatch this item is
  about.
- Evidence (2026-11-18, ContextHub epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9, child
  WL-0MWKY141H002LULI): two consecutive false reds in one session — attempt 1
  rebased in `508a1821e` (`isNotStarted`) → 17 × `TypeError: isNotStarted is not
  a function`; attempt 2 rebased in `ac2a2c48e` (`normalizeStartOn`) → multiple
  `TypeError: normalizeStartOn is not a function`. Both cleared with no source
  change: `git fetch origin dev && git rebase origin/dev && npm run build` →
  `finish` green. Direct proof of staleness: `grep -c normalizeStartOn
  packages/shared/dist/predicates.js` → `0` before the manual build, `2` after.

## Desired change

The item offers three mechanisms; research picks one as primary and one as a
cheap hardening, and records why the third cannot fix the defect alone.

**A — Rebuild after a recovery rebase (recommended, primary).** After the
successful `git rebase origin/dev` in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`, and
before the retry push, call `run_build(worktree_path)`. On failure, fail closed
(no retry push, failure comment naming the build stderr tail and the worktree,
item reset to `open`). Rationale: it makes the gate's subject and the build
consistent by construction, costs one build per rebase round (the rebase round
already costs a push attempt, and at most 5 rounds run), and needs no new
persistent state.

**B — Refuse to gate a tree newer than the last build (recommended hardening).**
Record the built tree SHA when the build succeeds (a `_set_finish_progress`
field / report field is enough — no new file format), and before a retry push
verify that `HEAD^{tree}` still matches it; when it does not, rebuild. This
generalises A to the other tree-changing paths that can precede a push (amend,
`git pull`, a rebase performed outside the recovery helper) at near-zero cost.
The fail-closed branch of the item's option 2 is therefore available as the
backstop without inventing a new abort source on the normal path.

**C — Rebuild-scoped cache key (rejected as a standalone fix).** The gate's key
is derived from the git tree (or the change-set patch), and `packages/shared/dist`
is gitignored, so a build-scoped key component could only be added by hashing a
build artifact into the key. That would invalidate verdicts for every unrelated
`finish` (every build produces a different `dist`), and it does not address the
actual defect: the suite *did* legitimately re-run, then failed on a stale
artifact. Keying cannot make an unbuilt tree built.

**Non-negotiable invariant (from the item):** whatever mechanism is implemented,
the push loop must never report a *source-level* test failure for a tree it did
not build.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`
  (~12262) gains the post-rebase rebuild (A) / built-tree check (B); the push
  loop in `phase_finish` (~13560–13660) surfaces the rebuild in
  `report["steps"]["push"]`; `run_build` (~9324) reused unchanged;
  `_set_finish_progress` (~759) carries the built-tree marker for B.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the existing
  non-fast-forward / load-flake harness (`_stubbed_finish`, `sandbox`) is the
  place for the AC1–AC5 tests.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — drop-in coverage for the
  recovery helper if the rebuild is asserted at helper level rather than through
  `phase_finish`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — the "A lost push race does not re-run
  the full suite" section (~2578) and the push-robustness list (~1715) need the
  post-rebase build documented alongside the change-set reuse they describe.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the false red is caused by a stale build artifact, not by a
  wrong `dev` merge. The evidence (`isNotStarted` / `normalizeStartOn` in source
  but absent from `dist`, cleared by `npm run build` alone) supports this; if a
  similar red survives a rebuild, it is a genuine regression and must stay red
  (AC3).
- **Risk — rebuild churn vs. the push-subject guard.** On game repos `npm run
  build` runs `engine:sync` first, which can advance the engine submodule and
  stage the pin/gitlink. `_assert_push_subject` refuses a push from a worktree
  with tracked uncommitted changes, so a churn-producing rebuild could turn a
  recoverable race into a `PushSubjectMismatchError`. Mitigation: snapshot the
  churn baseline before the post-rebase build (reusing `_build_churn_baseline`),
  attribute the churn as finish's own like Step 2 does, and fail closed with an
  actionable comment when the churn cannot be carried.
- **Risk — cost.** One extra build per rebase round (≤ `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT`
  = 5 rounds). Accepted: it is far cheaper than the observed false-red recovery,
  and it is not paid on the uncontended path (AC6).
- **Risk — masking.** A rebuild that *hides* a real failure would be worse than
  the bug. Mitigated by AC3's pin test and by keeping the gate's verdict
  untouched: the rebuild changes what the suite measures, never the pass/fail
  threshold.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Making the full-suite cache key build-aware
  (mechanism C), hardening the load-flake pattern list, or re-running the suite
  after every rebase are **out of scope**; each is either rejected above or worth
  its own item. Any such finding during implementation is recorded as a linked
  work item (`discovered-from:SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q`), not absorbed here.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVPI41SR008JYXL** (completed) — "Hard-fail finish on stale shared
  resolution": covers the *resolution* check (worktree `@worklog/shared` →
  main checkout's `dist`) but not the rebase-then-gate-without-rebuild ordering.
- **SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC** (completed) — "Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on
  dev pushes": its change-set reuse usually hides this defect; this item covers
  the miss case (upstream touched the same file, so the patch's pre-images
  differ) and the invariant that survives reuse.
- **SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG** (completed) — "Gate keys on the pushed tree": the
  provenance contract the rebuild must make honest.
- **SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5** (completed) — push robustness; its AC7 load-flake retry
  is the nearest existing mitigation and is deliberately narrow (load errors
  only), which is why this defect slips through it.
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** (completed) — worktree link-farm / stale dist parent of
  the stale-resolution work.
- Discovered from ContextHub **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (child WL-0MWKY141H002LULI);
  the two commits whose push triggered the rebases: ContextHub **WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV**,
  **WL-0MWMGEPY2004EDZ8**.

### Related work (automated `find-related` report)

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** (completed) – finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward
  after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly
  — same recovery path, sibling concern (refs, not build artefacts).
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** (completed) – Push to dev from the worktree that holds
  the commit — the push subject this item's rebuild must keep honest.
- **SA-0MWHUVISS003APKM** (open) – Tests: fresh-worktree shared build
  precondition (red-first): makes `start` ensure a worktree's
  `packages/shared/dist` is built. Complementary, not overlapping: it fixes
  freshness at *start*, this item fixes freshness after a *mid-push rebase*.
  Interfaces with it through the shared build helper and its
  `shared_build` report block.
- Repository file matches: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Which of the item's three mechanisms should the brief specify?**
  (Options: A rebuild-after-rebase; B record-the-built-tree / fail closed;
  C rebuild-scoped cache key.)
  **Recommended:** A as primary + B as hardening — A makes the gate's subject and
  the build consistent by construction for a bounded extra build per rebase
  round, B covers the other tree-changing paths cheaply; C alone cannot fix an
  unbuilt tree and would invalidate every unrelated verdict.
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** A + B described
  in *Desired change*; C rejected with rationale. The acceptance criteria are
  written behaviourally (the item's invariant) so the producer can substitute B
  alone or A alone without rewriting them. Source: repo research —
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`,
  `run_build`, `_is_gate_load_flake`), `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
  (`resolve_gate_subject`), `skill/test_cache.py`
  (`compute_change_set_state`), `.githooks/pre-push`, and
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` § "A lost push race does not re-run the
  full suite".
- **Q2: Is a post-rebase rebuild failure a hard stop or a consumed retry round?**
  **Recommended:** hard stop — a failed build is a content/config condition, not
  a transient transport one, so retrying the same tree cannot help (the same
  reasoning as the existing "load flake is retried, a reproducible failure
  blocks" split).
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** hard stop, per
  AC5. Source: `_is_retryable_push_transport` (`implement.py:6048`) and the
  Step 2 build-failure path (`implement.py:12786`).
- **Q3: Should the full suite re-run on the rebuilt tree even when the change-set
  verdict would be served from cache?**
  **Recommended:** no — keep the change-set reuse (it is a correctness argument
  about the patch, not about `dist`), because the rebuilt tree makes a real suite
  run (when one happens) trustworthy; re-running on every rebase would undo
  SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC's 5–18 min saving.
  **Answer (agent research, advisory until producer confirms):** keep reuse; the
  rebuild only guarantees that a *miss* is measured on a built tree. Source:
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` ~2578–2600.

## Goal

Red-first tests: pin the whole "never gate a tree you did not build" contract in
the existing `skill/implement` push-robustness harness **before** any production
change, so every later feature in this tree has a failing test to turn green.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC1a, AC1b, AC5, AC6, AC7).

## Scope

Tests only — no production change in this item. Extend the `sandbox` /
`_stubbed_finish` harness in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py`
(a scripted non-fast-forward recovery whose rebase introduces a new
`packages/shared` export while leaving `packages/shared/dist` stale) and, where
the assertion is cleaner at helper level, `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose recovery rebase introduces a new `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
- A test asserts the uncontended (no rejection) push path pays exactly one build per `finish`, and that the Step 3 changed-scope gate is never re-entered by the retry loop.
- A test asserts a failed post-rebase build produces no retry push, an actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the work item reset to `open`.
- A test asserts a stale-dist suite failure (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` on a tree whose `packages/shared/dist` predates the rebase) is never reported as a failure of the pushed change set: the run either rebuilds first or fails closed with a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
- Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no vacuous green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the existing `sandbox` fixture and the `_stubbed_finish` monkeypatch seams; add one shared helper that scripts "rebase advances `dev` with a new shared export and leaves `dist` stale".
- Stub `run_build` / `git_push_to_dev` / `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` with call-order recording so "build between rebase and retry push" is asserted from the observed order, not from a mock's return value.
- Record the failing-red run evidence in a comment on this item (test names + the assertion each fails on).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — main harness (`sandbox`, `_stubbed_finish`, test classes).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — helper-level assertions if the rebuild is asserted inside `_recover_non_fast_forward_push`.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — read-only reference (`_recover_non_fast_forward_push`, `run_build`, `_build_churn_baseline`).

## Deliverables

New/extended tests, all red against the current implementation, plus a comment
recording the red run.

## Dependencies

Blocks every implementation feature in this tree (test-first ordering).

## Goal

Rebuild the rebased worktree inside the push retry loop, so the retry push can
never reach the full-suite gate with a `packages/shared/dist` older than the
`dev` commits the rebase just pulled in.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC1, AC6, the rebuild half of AC2).

## Scope

`_recover_non_fast_forward_push` only, reusing the existing single build entry
point `run_build(cwd)` — no parallel build code path. No change to the gate's
pass/fail threshold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a successful recovery rebase inside the push loop, `finish` builds the rebased worktree before the retry push reaches the full-suite gate: `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` calls `run_build(worktree_path)` after the rebase and before `_assert_push_subject` / `git_push_to_dev`, and the run records the post-rebase build in `report["steps"]["push"]` so a simulated non-fast-forward rejection whose rebase introduces a new `packages/shared` export is reported green/pushed.
- Churn produced by the post-rebase build is attributed as finish's own: the churn baseline is snapshotted before the build (reusing `_build_churn_baseline`) so `_assert_push_subject` cannot refuse the retry push for churn finish itself caused.
- No extra build is paid when no rebase happened: the uncontended push path keeps exactly one build per `finish`, and the changed-scope gate (Step 3) is never re-entered by the retry loop.
- A build failure after the rebase does not reach the retry push (it delegates to the fail-closed path owned by the child "Fail closed when the post-rebase build fails").

## Minimal Implementation

- Call `run_build(worktree_path)` immediately after the rebase succeeds and the rewritten hash is captured, before `_assert_push_subject`.
- Surface the outcome as a `rebase_build` block on `report["steps"]["push"]` (attempt round, worktree, exit status, duration).
- Snapshot `_build_churn_baseline(worktree_path)` before the build and fold any new churn into the run's own-churn accounting, mirroring Step 2.
- Raise/re-raise the Step 2 build-failure exception shape on failure and let the caller handle the fail-closed transition.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (~12262), `run_build` (~9324), `_build_churn_baseline` (~4093), `_assert_push_subject`, push loop in `phase_finish` (~13560–13680).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the red-first tests this item turns green.

## Deliverables

The post-rebase rebuild, its report surface, churn attribution, and green tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Red-first tests: post-rebase rebuild contract".

## Goal

A post-rebase rebuild that itself fails must fail **closed**: no push, an
actionable comment, and the work item reset to `open` — never a gated unbuilt
tree.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC5).

## Scope

The failure branch of the post-rebase rebuild. Mirror the existing Step 2
build-failure path; do not consume a rebase/transport retry round.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A rebuild that fails after the rebase fails closed: no retry push is attempted for that round, and an actionable comment names the build failure (`stderr` tail) and the worktree path.
- The failure is a hard stop, not a retryable transport condition: `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` is untouched and no further rebase round runs against the same unbuildable tree.
- The work item is reset to `open` (mirroring the existing Step 2 build-failure path), never left `in-progress` with a stranded worktree.
- `report["steps"]["push"]` records the build failure (outcome, worktree, build stderr tail) so the failure is auditable after the fact.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the Step 2 build-failure classification and message shape; add the rebase round number and the retained worktree path.
- Call `wl_add_comment` with the stderr tail (bounded), then raise the same hard-stop exception class Step 2 raises so the leaf loop resets the item to `open`.
- Make sure the existing post-failure `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push` path still runs (local `dev` was deferred, never advanced).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` (~12262), Step 2 build-failure path (~12786), `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`, push loop (~13560–13680).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — the fail-closed assertions this item turns green.

## Deliverables

The fail-closed branch, its comment, the `open` reset, and green tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Red-first tests: post-rebase rebuild contract", "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push".

## Goal

Backstop the rebuild: a finish run knows which tree it built, and a gate
failure whose symptom is a stale shared build is diagnosed as a
build/resolution problem naming `packages/shared/dist` — never attributed to
the pushed change set.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC2, the hardening mechanism B).

## Scope

The built-tree marker + the stale-dist diagnosis. No change to the verdict
cache key (mechanism C is explicitly out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The finish run records the tree SHA (`HEAD^{tree}`) of the last successful build in the finish progress/report, and a HEAD tree that no longer matches it triggers a rebuild before any dev push — including the retry push — so no push ever gates an unbuilt tree; when that rebuild itself fails the run fails closed with a stale-build diagnosis naming `packages/shared/dist`.
- A gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function`, which the existing load-flake retry does not match because the module loads fine) is reported as a build/resolution diagnosis naming `packages/shared/dist`, never as a failure of the pushed change set.
- The guard adds no build on a tree that has not changed since the last build, and the changed-scope gate (Step 3) is never re-entered.
- Tests cover the stale-tree trigger, the unchanged-tree no-op, and the diagnosis wording.

## Minimal Implementation

- Record the built tree SHA via `_set_finish_progress` (an existing field surface — no new file format) when `run_build` succeeds in Step 2 and after the post-rebase rebuild.
- Before a dev push, compare `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` with the recorded value in the worktree; on mismatch rebuild (reusing `run_build`) and update the marker, or fail closed with the diagnosis when the rebuild fails.
- Classify a gate failure whose stderr tail matches the stale-shared symptom (`TypeError: <identifier> is not a function` where the identifier resolves from `packages/shared`) into the existing build/resolution diagnosis taxonomy instead of a change-set failure.
- Keep `_is_gate_load_flake` unchanged — this is a distinct symptom, not a load error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_set_finish_progress` (~759), `run_build` (~9324), `_is_gate_load_flake` (~6032), the push loop and gate-failure classification (~13560–13890).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_provenance.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — provenance + push-robustness tests.

## Deliverables

The built-tree marker, the freshness check, the stale-dist diagnosis, and tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push" (shares the post-rebase rebuild surface).

## Goal

Prove the user-visible outcome end to end: a `finish` whose push is rejected
once still lands its commit and writes the terminal transition with no manual
intervention, and a genuinely red rebased tree is still reported red.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC3, AC4, AC9).

## Scope

Verification only — end-to-end tests/checks over the behaviour delivered by the
other children in this tree; no new production mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `finish` on a worktree whose push is rejected once still lands the commit and writes the terminal `completed` / `in_review` transition, with no manual intervention (single end-to-end run against a sandbox worktree and a scripted remote).
- A genuine red introduced by the rebased commit is still reported red: when the rebased tree really fails the suite, the push is blocked and the item stays `open` (the rebuild does not weaken the gate).
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (run via the test skill / the dev-push gate), with no new failures.

## Minimal Implementation

- Drive the `sandbox` harness through a complete `finish` (rejection → rebase → rebuild → retry → terminal transition) and assert the transition status/stage and the landed commit.
- Add the genuine-red pin by making the rebased tree fail on a real assertion inside the suite stub; assert `PushGateFailureError`/gate reason and `open`.
- Run the full suite through `/skill:test` and attach the result to this item's comment (never an ad-hoc `pytest`).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — end-to-end push harness.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_provenance.py` — gate verdict/provenance assertions.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the suite entry point used by the gate (read-only reference).

## Deliverables

The end-to-end landing test, the genuine-red pin, and the green full-suite evidence.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push", "Fail closed when the post-rebase build fails", "Built-tree freshness guard and stale-dist diagnosis".

# Intake Brief — Standup report should not use "yesterday"/"today" language, and should avoid "On [topic]…" repetition (SA-0MWNGLPD4000829A)

**Headline:** Update `skill/standup/SKILL.md` so the daily standup report speaks
in time-neutral, varied prose — "since the last report" instead of "yesterday",
"key upcoming work includes" instead of "today" — and stops opening every
paragraph with the same "On [topic], …" template.

## Problem statement

The standup report's section headings and speech rules hard-code "yesterday"
and "today" language, and the worked example opens every clustered paragraph
with "On \<category\>, …". The result reads mechanically: the same temporal
frame is asserted even when the report window is not literally a day, and the
repeated "On X," opener is a clause template the report was meant to avoid.
A previous item (SA-0MWBRJ3KI006XJ46) was marked completed but its children
were never committed — `skill/standup/SKILL.md` still carries the old wording,
and `test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` still *requires* paragraphs to begin
with "On ".

## Users

- **The operator** who reads or listens to the daily standup across projects
  (SorraAgents, AI_Hell, ContextHub, Tableau-Card-Engine, games_curator).
- **TTS listeners** who hear the report read aloud — stock temporal phrases
  and identical paragraph openers sound robotic.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want the standup to describe completed work as happening
  *since the last report* rather than *yesterday*, so the wording matches the
  actual reporting window even when it is not a single day.
- As an operator, I want upcoming work framed as *key upcoming work includes*
  rather than *today*, so the report does not over-promise a one-day horizon.
- As a TTS listener, I want paragraph openers to vary naturally so the report
  does not sound like a repeated template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/standup/SKILL.md` contains no "yesterday" or "today" temporal
   framing in its section headings, speech rules, or worked example; completed
   work is framed as "since the last report" and upcoming work as "key
   upcoming work includes" (or close, natural equivalents).
2. The guidance explicitly directs the agent to vary paragraph openers — it no
   longer instructs that paragraphs must open with "On \<topic\>," and the
   worked example demonstrates varied openers (e.g. subject-first, verb-first,
   context-first) rather than a single repeated template.
3. `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` is updated to pin
   the new contract: the required section headings carry time-neutral wording,
   no "yesterday"/"today" tokens remain in those headings, and the example
   paragraphs are no longer required to start with "On "; a test asserts that
   the example's paragraph openers are varied (not all sharing one template).
4. `skill/standup/README.md` reflects the renamed section headings and the
   varied-opener guidance.
5. The change is documentation/contract only — `generate_standup.py` and its
   tests are unchanged (the script remains the deterministic data layer).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Verifiable
   check: a repository-wide grep for the old headings/phrases finds them only
   in the deterministic fallback renderer (`generate_standup.py` + its golden
   tests, out of scope per AC5) and in historical `standups/*.md` (never
   re-rendered).

## Impact

Standup reports read as natural, time-neutral prose with varied paragraph
openers — "since the last report" and "key upcoming work includes" replace the
stock yesterday/today framing, and the report no longer sounds like the same
"On [topic]…" template repeated paragraph after paragraph.

## Constraints

- Documentation/contract change only: no changes to `generate_standup.py` or
  its script tests — the script stays the deterministic data layer
  (SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2).
- Dated standup history (`standups/*.md`) is never re-rendered; only the skill
  docs and their pinning tests change.
- The change reaches every project via the global skill install
  (`scripts/install_pi.sh` refreshes `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup`); no
  per-project copy to maintain.
- Keep the fixed five-section order and the empty-section spoken lines; only
  the headings' temporal wording and the opener guidance change.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` § Report Rendering pins the section headings
  "### Yesterday I completed work on…" and "### Additional focus items for
  today", and the worked example opens every paragraph with "On
  \<category\>, …".
- `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` hard-codes those
  headings in `REPORT_HEADINGS` and in
  `test_example_paragraphs_open_with_a_spoken_category_label` asserts every
  paragraph `startswith("on ")`.
- `skill/standup/README.md` repeats the same heading names.
- SA-0MWBRJ3KI006XJ46 claimed to add a conversational-polish pass but its
  children were never committed; the SKILL.md and test still carry the old
  contract. The current item is the first real attempt at time-neutral,
  varied-opener wording.

## Desired change

- Rename the temporal section headings to time-neutral phrasing (e.g.
  "### Since the last report, I completed…" and "### Key upcoming work
  includes…"), keeping all five sections in order.
- Replace the speech-rule examples "Yesterday I completed…" / "My focus
  today is…" with "Since the last report I completed…" / "My key upcoming
  work includes…" (or natural equivalents).
- Replace the "On \<category\>, …" opener mandate with guidance to vary
  openers naturally, and update the worked example to show varied openers.
- Update the pinning test to enforce the new headings and varied openers.
- Update `skill/standup/README.md` to match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` — rename temporal section headings, update speech
  rules and the worked example, replace the "On [topic]" opener mandate with
  varied-opener guidance.
- `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` — update
  `REPORT_HEADINGS`, the section-order test, the opener test, and add a test
  that the example's paragraph openers are varied.
- `skill/standup/README.md` — reflect renamed headings and varied-opener
  guidance.

## Related work

- SA-0MWBRJ3KI006XJ46 (completed, but phantom — children never committed) —
  "More conversational standup reports"; this item completes the
  opener-variation half that was declared out of scope there.
- SA-0MW6EUVGM009RMD2 (completed) — established the agent-rendered clustered
  contract this change refines.
- SA-0MW6ER1NX0094QCG (open) — "Standup more focused on user experience";
  adjacent quality goal, different scope.
- SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ (completed) — project title in the standup header.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the temporal wording change applies to the section headings
  as well as the narrative prose — the headings are the most visible
  "yesterday"/"today" references. If the producer wants headings left
  unchanged, the scope shrinks to prose only.
- **Assumption:** "Open critical items", "Regressions" and "Blockers" keep
  their names — they carry no temporal language.
- **Risk:** changing the pinned headings is a breaking contract change for the
  test suite; the test update must land in the same change.
- **Risk:** "varied openers" is prose guidance to an LLM, so output quality
  varies by model; the pinning test checks the *documented contract* (no
  repeated template in the example), not generated prose (accepted — the
  render is agent-authored by design).
- **Scope-creep guard:** further opportunity (e.g. a per-project voice, richer
  conversational-polish pass) is recorded as a linked work item, not folded
  into this change.

## Plan review notes (plan skill skip-path review)

- **Residual temporal prose in SKILL.md.** Beyond the headings, speech rules and
  worked example named in AC1, `skill/standup/SKILL.md` still says "Today's
  focus list includes all open critical items…" (selection rule) and "if the
  Herdr window is empty, today is empty". Reword these for a consistent
  time-neutral voice.
- **Do NOT rename the JSON data-contract keys.** `yesterday_items`,
  `today_critical_items` and `today_additional_items` are the deterministic
  data layer (`generate_standup.py`); only the prose changes.
- **Atomic commit.** `SKILL.md`, `tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py` and
  `README.md` must change in the same commit — the pinning test fails if either
  side lands alone (see AC3 + Risk).
- **README constraints.** `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_help_docs.py`
  requires the README to keep mentioning `SKILL.md` and `generate_standup.py`
  and to keep the grouped/impact-first vocabulary — preserve those when
  renaming the five section names.
- **Documentation sweep result (AC7).** Only `skill/standup/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/standup/README.md`, `skill/standup/tests/test_skill_md_clustered_report.py`,
  the fallback renderer's golden tests and historical `standups/*.md` mention
  the old headings; `docs/` has no standup-format page, so no docs-site edit is
  needed.
- **Recorded divergence (out of scope, follow-up filed).** The deterministic
  fallback `format_report()` keeps its yesterday/today headings per AC5, so
  scheduled non-agent runs will speak the old framing — tracked as
  SA-0MWNMRCYY0050LEP (discovered-from this item).
- **Vertical-slice check:** single small documentation/contract slice with no
  layer phasing needed; no children created (effort Small / risk Low, below the
  planning threshold).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the repeated 'On [topic]…' opener be fixed by (A) freeing the
  agent to vary openers with guidance + a varied example, or (B) mandating a
  fixed rotation of opener templates?" — Answer (agent, seed context): **A —
  free variation with guidance and a varied example**; the seed context asks
  for "more conversational and varied", not a mechanical rotation. Source:
  work-item description supplied by the producer. No blocking question.
- Q2: "Do the section headings change, or only the narrative prose?" —
  Assumption (agent, documented above): **headings change too** — the seed
  context's "instead of referring to yesterday … should say something like
  'since the last report'" is most visible in the headings. Flagged for
  producer confirmation at review; not blocking.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWJEFXW5003M7W1** – Extend test to pin the second-iteration contract (completed)
- **SA-0MWBRJ3KI006XJ46** – More conversational standup reports (completed)
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** – Fix legacy skill/ path reference in planall SKILL.md (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, accepted, actual, add, additional (+233 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: acceptance, accepted, actual, add, additional (+218 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, accepted, actual, add, additional (+209 more)

### Plan review addendum (plan skill skip-path, 2026-11-19)

- Q (agent, review stage 1): "Should the deterministic fallback renderer
  (`format_report`) also adopt the time-neutral headings?" — Not answered here;
  AC5 and the Constraints explicitly exclude `generate_standup.py` and its
  tests from this change, so the conservative call is to leave it untouched and
  record the divergence as **OPEN QUESTION** for producer review at the next
  planning horizon, tracked as SA-0MWNMRCYY0050LEP (priority low). Non-blocking
  because the item's scope is the agent-rendered narrative only.
- Q (agent, review stage 5): "Is AC7 measurable?" — Refined with a grep-based
  verifiable check; intent unchanged.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles
- Failing commit: 6dafa2d4d983ef9e4df6cffc7f20152e1b85e730
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
def test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles() -> None:
        """Live syntax check: the committed template must produce no parse errors.
    
        Runs ``systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run`` against the template.  The
        dry-run never modifies the filesystem.  Parse failures surface as
        ``Invalid …`` diagnostics on stderr (e.g. a mistyped age or missing
        field); the exit code alone is not asserted because unprivileged runs
        report unrelated permission errors (e.g. root-owned private dirs).
    
        Skipped when the binary is unavailable (e.g. non-systemd hosts).
        """
        binary = shutil.which("systemd-tmpfiles")
        if binary is None:
            import pytest
    
            pytest.skip("systemd-tmpfiles not available on this host")
    
>       proc = subprocess.run(
            [
                binary,
                "--clean",
                "--dry-run",
                "--graceful",
                "--exclude-prefix=/tmp/snap
```

## Root Cause

The test runs `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` against the real `/tmp`, which contains ~538k inodes. Under host load this can take >120s (the test's timeout budget), causing `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` before any parse assertion is reached. The audit session confirmed: the identical command on this host takes 12.8s idle; under suite+parallel load it exceeds 120s.

## Plan

**Fix:** Replace `--clean` with `--root=/tmp/pi-probe-root` (a synthetic empty directory) in the subprocess call. This runs systemd-tmpfiles against an empty filesystem tree — the template path is still parsed and validated (same parsing path as `--clean`), but no /tmp directories are scanned, so the call completes in ~5ms regardless of host load. Verified: `--root` correctly detects parse errors (\"Unknown command type\", \"Invalid age\") in synthetic templates.

**Changed file:** `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` — one-line edit to the `subprocess.run()` call in `test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles`.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 6dafa2d4d983ef9e4df6cffc7f20152e1b85e730`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

The suite no longer stalls for minutes or times out when run on a loaded host — the tmpfiles syntax check now completes in milliseconds, so users can trust the test result instead of dismissing it as a flake.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

# ruff ISC004 False-Positive Evaluation — `measure_slot_wait.py:717`

## Problem

Ruff reports ISC004 ("Unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection") on `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py:717` (and 11 similar instances across two files). The audit created a chore work item requiring producer decision on whether to accept the finding or fix the code.

## Users

- **Developer/CI pipeline:** Wants clean lint output without false-positive noise.
- **Code reviewer:** Needs ISC004 to remain meaningful for catching genuine comma-forgotten bugs.

## Analysis

The flagged code builds report-summary strings inside a list literal:

```python
lines = [
    f"corpus: root={report['sessions_root']} "
    f"files_scanned={report['files_scanned']} "
    f"files_with_samples={report['files_with_samples']} "
    f"records_in_window={report['records_in_window']} "
    f"samples={report['total_samples']}",
]
```

Each list element is a **logical output line** composed of multiple f-string fragments joined by Python's implicit string concatenation. The elements are **correctly comma-separated** — there is no missing comma. The trailing comma on each element makes the list structure unambiguous.

The same pattern appears 12 times across two files (`measure_slot_wait.py`, `measure_finish_contention.py`), all in `render_summary`-style functions building human-readable report output.

**Conclusion: this is a false positive.** The ISC004 rule triggers on any adjacent strings inside a collection, even when the collection structure (commas) makes the intent unambiguous. The code is correct; ruff's heuristic is overly aggressive here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The ISC004 finding is accepted as a false positive (waiver added, work item resolved).
2. All 12 ISC004 instances across the two files are covered by a single waiver (rule ISC004, applicable files, justification that each element is intentionally comma-separated in a list of report-line fragments).
3. The ruff rule remains active for all other code paths (not globally disabled).

## Impact

The CI pipeline produces clean lint output without suppressing ruff's ISC004 rule for code that genuinely needs it.

## Constraints

- Waiver must be scoped (file-specific or rule-specific with justification), not a blanket disable.
- ISC004 must remain enforced for all other files and contexts.

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — `render_summary()` function
- `scripts/measure_finish_contention.py` — multiple `render_summary` functions
- `ruff.toml` or `pyproject.toml` — ruff configuration

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The waiver scope must be precise; over-scoping could mask real comma-forgotten bugs.
- **Mitigation:** Scope waiver to the specific files or add `# noqa: ISC004` inline comments at each location.
- **Assumption:** No other team members are modifying these patterns in new code without awareness.
- **Scope creep:** This task is limited to evaluating the specific finding; new ISC004 findings in other files are separate items.

## Appendix

- Q: "Is there a comma between adjacent strings on lines 715-716 or 717-721?" — Answer (agent): No — but that is intentional. Each pair of adjacent f-strings forms a single list element; the element itself is comma-separated from its neighbours. This is Python's standard implicit string concatenation, not a missing comma. Source: code inspection of `measure_slot_wait.py:714-722`.

## Problem

SA-0MWNGLPD4000829A makes the *agent-authored* standup narrative time-neutral
(`### Since the last report, I completed…` / `### Key upcoming work includes…`
and varied paragraph openers). Its AC5 deliberately leaves the deterministic
fallback renderer unchanged, so the two renderers will diverge:

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py::format_report` still emits
  `### Yesterday I completed work on...` and
  `### Additional focus items for today` (plus the line
  `No additional items — my focus today is entirely on critical work.`).
- `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_golden_report.py` and
  `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_impact_render.py` pin those
  headings.
- `skill/standup/README.md` § Fallback rendering therefore documents
  headings the agent-rendered report no longer uses.

Scheduled/non-agent runs (the documented fallback path) keep the stock
temporal framing the producer asked to remove.

## User story

As an operator, I want scheduled non-agent standup runs to speak with the same
time-neutral framing as agent-rendered reports, so the fallback is not a
second, older-sounding voice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `format_report` emits the same time-neutral headings as `skill/standup/SKILL.md`.
- The golden-report and impact-render tests are updated to pin the new headings.
- `skill/standup/README.md` § Fallback rendering matches the rendered output.
- Full project test suite passes.

## Decision — producer confirmed (2026-11-19)

The fallback **adopts** the agent-facing time-neutral contract: `format_report`
follows `skill/standup/SKILL.md` rather than staying frozen for back-compat
consumers. This settles the inherited open question from SA-0MWNGLPD4000829A;

the fallback headings, historical `standups/*.md` are never re-rendered, and
the JSON data-contract keys (`yesterday_items`, `today_critical_items`,
`today_additional_items`) are untouched either way.

One vertical slice; no child work items (Extra Small / Low — below the
decomposition threshold, so test-first ordering is applied inside the slice:
pinning tests change with the renderer in the same commit).

   survives in `format_report` output.
4. `skill/standup/README.md` § Fallback rendering — state that the fallback

5. Verification: run the standup tests through the test skill (`/skill:test`,

Extra Small (~2.3 h recommended, 1.6–3.4 h range), Low risk. Recorded by the
effort-and-risk skill.

- **Polish & handoff** — exact old/new strings recorded so implementation is

  re-rendered. No further questions block planning or implementation.

# Problem statement

Ruff reports two ISC004 findings in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` at lines 715 and 717 — unparenthesised implicit string concatenation within a list literal. The description frames these as a "candidate false positive" because the concatenation is intentional, but the lint rule is designed to catch exactly this pattern since missing commas would silently merge list elements.

# Users

- Developer experience: clean lint passes with no noise from legitimate patterns.
- Code quality: consistent ISC004 resolution across the repo (precedent: parenthesise, not waive).

# Acceptance Criteria

1. `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` passes `ruff check --isolated --select ISC004` with zero findings.
2. All existing tests for `measure_slot_wait.py` continue to pass (`pytest tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py`).
3. Script output is functionally identical (verified by re-running with representative corpus data).

# Impact

Lint runs over the slot-wait measurement harness now report zero ISC004 findings, so contributors stop having to judge whether the flagged implicit string concatenation is a missing comma or a deliberate multi-line string, and a future missing comma can no longer slip through silently.

# Constraints

- Must follow repo precedent: ISC004 findings are resolved by parenthesising implicit string concatenation, not by waiving (see fix commit `db14a6897a`, `981af4d849`).
- No code behaviour change — only syntax-level restructuring.

Two ISC004 errors reported by ruff in `render_summary()` function at lines 715–721. The implicit concatenation builds list elements for `lines.append(...)`:

Wrap the implicitly concatenated f-string groups in parentheses so ruff recognises them as single expressions rather than potential missing-comma errors.

# Problem statement

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_changed_flag'` when it is run against a repository with **zero detected test suites**. `state_changed_flag` is initialised inside `for cmd in commands:` (run_suite), so when `commands == []` the loop body never executes and the post-loop reference (`if state_changed_flag:`) reads an unbound local.

# Users

- **CI/CD pipeline** — the dev-push pre-push hook runs `run_tests.py --scope full` as the full-suite gate; a greenfield repo cannot push without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.
- **Developers** — running `run_tests.py` by hand on a freshly initialised repo.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `run_tests.py --scope full --json` on a repo with no detected suites exits 0 with a defined no-suites verdict instead of crashing.
- AC2: A greenfield repo with only `.githooks` can pass the dev-push gate without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.
- AC3: Unit tests cover the zero-suite path (`run_suite` per-suite and `run_all` aggregate), asserting the machine-readable no-suites signal.
- AC4: Documentation is updated — code comments, the `test` skill page (`skill/test/SKILL.md`) and the relevant `docs/dev/` reference.
- AC5: The full project test suite passes with the change.

# Impact

Newly initialised repositories (and any repo whose tooling yields no suites) get a clean, machine-readable "no test suites detected" verdict and can push through the standard gate instead of tripping over a runner crash or needing the documented bypass.

# Constraints

- Fix lives in the shared runner `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (no project-local override).
- Repos with one or more suites must be unaffected (regression-safe): the empty-command verdict is additive.

# Desired change

- Initialise `state_changed_flag` before the `for cmd in commands:` loop so the post-loop reference is always bound.
- Return an early, clean verdict for the zero-command case: `success=True`, `returncode=0`, `notice_code=NOTICE_NO_SUITES_DETECTED`, `notice="no test suites detected ..."`, `cached=False`, empty failure lists.
- Register `NOTICE_NO_SUITES_DETECTED` beside the other `NOTICE_*` constants; document it in the test skill page.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — guard + constant.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_zero_suites.py` — new unit tests.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (or nearest reference) — docs.

# Related work

- Code half of `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (games_curator worklog: "run_tests.py crashes on greenfield repo with zero test suites"); that item tracks the greenfield bootstrap that surfaced the crash.
- Supersedes an earlier uncommitted attempt (0MWIBGLIL00774EU) whose working-tree edit was overwritten by later `run_tests.py` commits — this item commits the fix so it cannot evaporate again.

## User story

As an agent operating under the global guidance, I should be told explicitly that I am the owner and long-term maintainer of the codebase and that its design is my responsibility, so that I maintain long-term design health instead of only satisfying the immediate task.

## Background

Neither the global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (installed as `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) nor `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` currently states anything equivalent to "you are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you".

The gap is not neutral — the existing tone actively reads the other way:

- `Coding Disciplines` items 2 and 3 ("Simplicity First", "Surgical Changes") are preservationist and, unqualified, discourage design work beyond the task.
- `Surgical Changes` explicitly says dead code is *mentioned, not deleted*, which defers maintenance indefinitely.
- The refactor skill describes itself as automated smell detection and work-item filing — hygiene performed by a tool, not stewardship exercised by an owner.

The consequence is that agents defer design responsibility: they report smells and file items rather than fixing what they touch, and they do not treat design coherence as their own problem.

## Proposed changes

### 1. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` → `## Coding Disciplines`

- Amend item 3 (`Surgical Changes`) so dead code is *reported via a work item, or folded into the current one*, rather than silently deleted — i.e. it becomes a handled decision instead of an indefinite deferral.
- Add item 6, `**Codebase Ownership**`:

  > You are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you. Judge each change by the long-term health of the whole, not just by whether the immediate task compiles: maintain coherent abstractions, and leave the code better than you found it. Ownership is exercised *through* the workflow, not around it — a redesign still lands as a work item implemented via `/skill:implement`, still respects the repository boundaries in (4), and still ships with tests. Ownership is authority over *design*, never over *process*.

  The final two sentences are load-bearing: without them the clause reads as licence for unbounded redesign and contradicts items 2, 3 and 4 plus the worktree / finish gates. The clause grants design judgement, not process exemption.

### 2. `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` → new `### Ownership mindset` section after `## Overview`

Drafted text makes existing behaviour legible as ownership (fixing smells inside code you are already changing is part of the work, not scope creep), while restating that smells outside session scope still become work items, fixes still pass the test gate, and redesign lands through `/skill:implement`.

## Trade-offs considered

- **Risk of unbounded refactoring.** Mitigated by tying ownership to the workflow (work item + implement skill + test gate).
- **Conflict with `Simplicity First`.** Left adjacent and reconciled by wording in item 6 ("judged by the long-term health of the whole"). The stronger alternative — rewording item 2 to explicitly balance against whole-system design — was considered and deferred: item 6 carries that job without two edits to the same principle set.
- **Stronger wording option** (ownership outranks simplicity) is deliberately not taken, to avoid weakening the anti-speculation guard that keeps agent changes reviewable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` `## Coding Disciplines` contains an ownership principle that states, in substance, that the agent is the owner and long-term maintainer of the codebase and that its design is its responsibility.
- [ ] The ownership principle explicitly bounds itself: design authority, not process exemption; workflow (work item, implement skill, tests) and repository boundaries still apply.
- [ ] `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` item 3 (`Surgical Changes`) no longer defers dead code indefinitely — it names a handling path.
- [ ] `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` contains an `### Ownership mindset` section that frames refactoring as maintenance performed by an owner, and states that ownership does not bypass the workflow (out-of-scope smells still become work items; the test gate still applies).
- [ ] The two documents are consistent with each other and do not contradict existing principles in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
- [ ] No functional change to any skill script; changes are prose only.
- [ ] Full test suite passes (prose-only change, but the gate applies).
- [ ] After merge to `dev`, the operator is told to re-run `scripts/install_pi.sh` so `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` picks up the change (the installed copy is a symlink/export from this repository).

## Out of scope

- Re-running `scripts/install_pi.sh` as part of this item (it is an operator step after merge).
- Retro-establishing the principle in other skills (implement, plan, audit) — separate item if wanted.

## Notes

- Both target files are repository-boundary protected (`skill/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); this item is the explicit instruction that authorises the edit.
- Prose-only change: no new tests required, but existing skill-doc/lint tests must stay green.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W** – Split global vs project AGENTS.md: AGENTS_GLOBAL.md canonical source + symlink install (completed)
- **SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G** – SorraAgents AGENTS.md: reference global instead of duplicating 20KB (completed)
- **SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP** – Compact AGENTS_GLOBAL.md to ≤8 KB (F4) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, actively, add, adjacent, agent (+188 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: acceptance, add, adjacent, agent, agents (+177 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, actively, add, agent, agents (+171 more)

# Problem statement

`audit_runner.py issue <id> --code-root <CODE_REPO>` (cross-repo audit, LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR) builds the Phase 1/Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest from the **code root**, then validates it against the **worklog owning root**, so validation always fails for a genuine cross-repo item — and the parent AC screen aborts with a scope error, leaving the persisted report with an **empty Acceptance Criteria table** while still recording `Ready to close: No`.

# Reproduction (verified 2026-11-19)

Item `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (worklog: games_curator, code: SorraAgents at `0c41811c67`):

```bash
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --force \
  --code-root /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
```

Log (`~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`):

```
[checkpoint] Phase 1 parent screening started
Error: Audit scope error: the Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest does not contain the work item repository files (owning project: /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator). The resolved scope is the audit skill's own tree or another repository; re-launch the audit from /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator and re-run.
[checkpoint] Phase 1 child screenings started
```

# Root cause

- `_phase_parent_screen` builds the manifest with `project_root=ctx.execution_root` (the code root) — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~line 15375.
- It then calls `_validate_file_scope_manifest(file_scope, owning_root, touched_files=...)` (~line 15383) — the worklog owner, not the code root. `_validate_file_scope_manifest` compares `_distinctive_project_top_levels(owning_root)` against the manifest text, so a manifest legitimately built from the code repo can never contain the worklog repo's distinctive top-level entries.
- The same mismatch exists in the Phase 2 path (~line 11230, `owning_root = _resolve_owning_project_root(...)` when `owning_root is None`).
- Secondary defect: the phase-1 scope error is printed and the screen returns 1, but `audit_runner()` continues into child screening / Phase 2 and persists a report whose AC table is empty — a fail-closed scope error should abort the run (non-zero exit, no persisted verdict) per the skill contract, never persist an AC-less verdict.
- The skill documentation already specifies that `--code-root` scopes "the file-scope manifest": only the validation root was left un-threaded.

# Desired change

- When `--code-root` / `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` resolves a code root, validate the FILE SCOPE manifest against **that** root (i.e. the per-audit/code root, same value used to build it), keeping the owning root as the validation root only when no code root is given.
- Treat a Phase 1 parent-screen scope error as fatal for the run: abort before persisting any report, restore the pre-audit lifecycle, exit non-zero.
- Keep same-repo behaviour byte-for-byte identical (`--code-root <owning-root>` remains a no-op).

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A cross-repo item audited with `--code-root` reaches Phase 1 parent AC screening with no `Audit scope error`, and the persisted report contains one row per AC (non-empty `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table).
- AC2: A same-repo item audited with `--code-root <owning-root>` yields an identical manifest, validation outcome and verdict to the same audit without `--code-root` (regression-safe).
- AC3: A genuine mis-scoped launch (manifest built from the audit skill's own tree) still fails closed.
- AC4: A Phase 1 parent-screen scope error aborts the run with a non-zero exit, persists no audit report, and leaves the item's pre-audit status/stage restored.
- AC5: Unit tests cover the cross-repo validation root, the same-repo no-op and the fatal-abort path; the full project suite passes.

# Evidence

- Failing run log: `~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`
- Persisted report with empty AC table: `wl --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator/.worklog audit-show CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --json`

# Impact

Cross-repo work items can be audited with real acceptance-criteria verdicts instead of a report that says "not ready" without ever assessing a criterion.

# Related work

- discovered-from: `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU`
- Sibling defect: the F3 execution worktree is likewise hosted under the worklog owner (filed separately).
- Feature that introduced `--code-root`: LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR.
